Project lens, checked against the source. The change touches no protected, generated or raster-timed line, and no data. It is scroll_screen_right in game.6502: main RAM, running as game logic. crtc_start_address_high/low (&B0/&B1) have one name each in zp.6502. The vsync interrupt never reads them: it uses flip_crtc_hi/lo, which the renderer copies. The renderer's save_game_zp/restore_game_zp save &B0/&B1 around the render, and the render never runs inside this code. So nothing can see the new store order (low before high) half-done. Every writer keeps the high byte in &08-&0F: reset_screen_scroll sets &08, this code and the left scroll wrap to &08/&0F, and buffer_to_view/history_to_view copy those values or zeroed slots (0). The one case where old and new differ, &10 on entry, never happens, and the carry case wraps the same way. X and Y are dead after. layers_right writes Y first and writes X (in get_scenery_address_for_layer_Y) before any read. change_pixel_tables uses neither. After install_prebuilt, layers_right_done writes Y (LDY #1) and add_ground_to_column_buffer writes X first. The callers (main loop, observer mode, scroll_into_world) get the registers the tail leaves, which have not changed. V is untouched on both paths, and C is not live at the dispatch. install_prebuilt returns to the BRA with the same A=Y=&FF, C=1, N=1, Z=0 and the same stack depth. The walk returns to JMP layers_right_done, which takes 3 cycles like the BRA. The removed labels have no other references. layers_right, which prebuild_layers calls, keeps its address because the window stays 31 bytes (recounted: both 31). There is no paging dependence: the code reads only zero page and pre_use (&2F32, main RAM). Recount, prebuilt path with no carry: old 63 cycles, new 46, so 17 fewer. Walk path: 14 fewer. skeptics.reason: Checked every entry and exit. Entries: consider_mover_firing_bullet is reached by JSR from update_mover (4579) and by JMP from update_enemy_helicopter (4387). check_for_target_behind_mover, found_target_3110 and set_firing_frame have no references outside this routine. No label+N operand points into the window, there are no literal addresses in &2B90-&2F52, and nothing branches into 4533-4538. No-target path: old BCS at &2BB8 is taken to &2C17, a page crossing, so 4 cycles. New BCC is not taken (2 cycles) and runs the same LDY mover_to_update / LDA movers_frame_and_flip,Y (&1322+Y, the same cost) / STA &B7 / RTS. So the registers, N/Z, C=1 and V are identical, the stack is the same and it returns to the same caller. Target-behind path: BCC is taken to &2BC0, same page, 3 cycles against 2 before. That is +1 on a path measured at 0.0 a pass, and the state is identical. Removed second JSR: Y is still mover_to_update from the first JSR. STA movers_firing_cooldown-1,Y writes &1254+Y (Y is 1-11, mover_to_update can be &0A/&0B for helicopters), so it never aliases &03, &B7 or movers_frame_and_flip at &1322. X is untouched by the subroutine, so CPX #&05 gives the same N, Z and C. Only A differs on the helicopter exit (BCS leave_with_carry_clear_315f; CLC; RTS), and A is dead there. update_mover's caller does DEC/BPL then LDX/LDA or LDA helicopter_to_update. update_enemy_helicopter's only caller (3310) goes on to JSR render_pass, which starts LDA #&04. The soldier path reloads A with LDA firing_frame and then reads &B7, which is unchanged. Interrupt: irq1_handler and sfx_tick write only VIA, CRTC, ULA, ACCCON, field_count, game_over_cooldown, shown_screen and their own sfx variables, never &03, &B7 or the mover tables. Bytes: the change adds 8 (LDY zp, LDA abs,Y, STA zp, RTS) and removes 3 (the JSR), so it grows by 5: -5 in the ledger's bytes-saved convention, which matches the claim.

The window itself is right on the machine. BCS &2BB8 to &2C17 is taken across a page (4 cycles); the new BCC is not taken (2). The inlined LDY zp / LDA abs,Y / STA zp / RTS costs the same as before, and every opcode is NMOS-legal. The code grows 8-3 = 5 bytes, and BNE leave_3160 at &2B9B goes to an offset of +126, which still reaches.

What is wrong is the slide check. The claim checked crossings only in &2BBA-&2F4D, against pc profiles from 14:07 that have no hits at all in &2F4D-&3348. Yet the current source puts kindcache_build there, and render calls JSR kc_build every pass. That region also moves by 5 bytes, and it holds kc_slot0_y (KC_Y0, 257 bytes, SKIP KC_CAP0). It moves from &3247 to &324C in the SHIFT 0 build and from &324B to &3250 in the bench build. kc_draw.yo and kc_restore.ryo read it with a self-modified LDY &FFFF,X, the operand set to KC_Y0-1+kc_off, with X counting each group down to 1. An entry costs +1 when it sits in the page after its group's base. In SHIFT 0 the &3300 page boundary falls at index &B9 in the old build and &B4 in the new; in the bench build it is &B5 against &B0. Sprite &15 is the 257-byte 12-column kind slot 0 is sized for, and its indices &B4-&B9 almost certainly fall in the same group (5 groups of about 51 entries). So each draw and each restore of a slot-0 part gains 5 crossings: about 10 cycles a pass while such a part is on screen. That is more than the 2.7 cycles a pass claimed, and nothing measured it: passlock checks state, not cycles, and passbench was not run.

The slide also makes two rare paths cost +1 cycle that the claim does not mention. In SHIFT 0, BCS set_frame_and_flip_3149 (&2BC4 -> &2BCC, target &2C04) starts crossing a page. In the bench build, BCC replot_mover at &2BC4 does too. Separately, the BCC to found_target_behind_w1a is now taken (3 cycles instead of 2) on the target-found-behind path. Other crossings change too and are not in the claim: in SHIFT 0, BRA count_column (&2FFB), BCS not_cachable (&3011) and BPL unflipped (&30FD) stop crossing; in the bench build, BNE row (&3248) stops crossing and BNE not_sam (&2CF1) starts.

The net cycle effect of the 5-byte slide over the kind cache is unmeasured and plausibly negative, so the claim does not stand as made. It would stand only if the slide were absorbed before kindcache_build (or kc_slot0_y were pinned), or if passbench showed no loss.

Only N/Z differ at exit, and both callers (1134, 1287) do LDA scenery_layer_sprite_addresses_high,Y next, which sets them again. Stack: the same at every exit. Interrupt: irq1_handler (4093-4180) and sfx_tick touch only VIA/CRTC/ULA registers, field/flip variables and sfx_* in bank 5/&29D4, never &CE/&CF or the scenery tables, so seeing the low byte written before the high one makes no difference. Bytes: 27 old, 27 new. Cycles recounted from the JSR return: positive 59 -> 31 (saves 28), negative 68 -> 42 (saves 26); (60*28+6*26)/66 = 27.8.

Machine lens holds. LDA (zp) (B2, 5 cycles) is a real 65SC12 opcode and Baron already assembles it in the game's section (LDA (kg_col) at &313E is B2 1F); no Rockwell bit ops. Recount from &1821 on, after the shared LDA abs,Y/TAY/JSR move_to_next_column_in_XY: old positive = STA abs,Y 5 + TXA 2 + STA abs,Y 5 + JSR 6 + use_scenery_sprite_address_for_layer_Y 24 (LDA abs,Y 4, LDX abs,Y 4, TAY 2, STX zp 3, STY zp 3, LDY # 2, RTS 6; tables at &10A1/&1099, read with Y=edge_and_layer, no crossing) + LDA (zp),Y 5 (Y=0, no crossing) + BPL taken 3 (&182D->&1832, same page) + LDY zp 3 + RTS 6 = 59; new = 5+3+2+5+3+LDA (zp) 5+BMI not taken 2+RTS 6 = 31 (saves 28). Old negative = 5+2+5+6+24+5+BPL 2+TYA 2+BEQ taken 3+LDY 3+STA abs,Y 5+RTS 6 = 68; new = 5+3+2+5+3+5+BMI taken 3+LDA # 2+BEQ taken 3+STA abs,Y 5+RTS 6 = 42 (saves 26). Writes take no index penalty. Layout by hand: &181A LDA abs,Y(3) &181D TAY &181E JSR(3) &1821 STA abs,Y(3) &1824 STA zp(2) &1826 TXA &1827 STA abs,Y(3) &182A STA zp(2) &182C LDA (zp)(2) &182E BMI(2, to &1831) &1830 RTS &1831 LDA #0(2) &1833 BEQ(2) -> ends &1835 = add_ground_to_column_buffer, unchanged: 27 bytes old and new, nothing after moves. BEQ offset &1816-&1835 = -&1F = E1, lands on STA scenery_layer_sprite_addresses_high,Y (listing &1816) inside page &18, 3 cycles taken; BMI +1 within page, 3 taken. Self-modifying code: the only patched operands near here are use_flipped_or_unflipped_scenery_sprite_opcode_two at &17F1 (written at game.6502 1079/1373, saved and restored by prebuild.6502), outside the block and not moved; the JMP at &17F3 still targets &181A. No other reference (label or numeric &181A-&1834) to the block in src/, and no code reads this page as data. &CE/&CF are not touched by irq1_handler or sfx_tick, and the store order changes nothing the CPU could see. Weighted from the stated counts (60 x 28 + 6 x 26)/66 = 27.8.

    INY
    LDA (scenery_sprite_address),Y

.filln

ucn_run_end = * + 1
    CPX #0                          \ operand set above (self-modified: HAZEL is RAM)
    BNE filln
    LDY scenery_data_offset
    JMP next
.skipn
    LDX ucn_run_end
    JMP next
.mergen
    STA scenery_mask

.mergen_loop

    STA column_buffer,X
    INX

    BNE mergen_loop

    JMP next
summary: The long run's end offset goes into the fill loop's CPX as a self-modified immediate (STA abs at line 216) instead of zero page &F8. The fill loop's CPX zp (3 cycles) becomes CPX # (2), saving 1 cycle per byte filled. The store, skipn's LDX and mergen's CPX each use the operand absolute, which costs +1 cycle and +1 byte each. Net about 0.3 cycles a pass, 3 bytes larger.
equivalence: filln, skipn and mergen are local to the unpack_scenery_column scope and referenced nowhere else in src/. All three are reached only through line 216, which now writes the same value (A = X + n) to the CPX's operand that it used to write to &F8. Every later read in the run (the fill's CPX, skipn's LDX, mergen_loop's CPX) reads that operand. So X, A, Y and the flags are the same at every exit (JMP next with the same X and Y): CPX #v and CPX abs set NZC as CPX zp does for the same v, and LDX abs sets flags as LDX zp does. The operand is rewritten before every read, because each long run passes line 216 first. So its initial #0 never matters, and prebuild/pre_undo need not save it: it carries nothing between runs. &F8 (end_of_run_offset / mover_x_low) is now left holding n (line 212's store) instead of X + n. The routine's header and prebuild.6502's measurement both say nothing reads it after the walk before writing it, and prebuild saves and restores it as before. move_to_next_column sets every flag it leaves (ADC, LDY), so no other difference can be seen.
relies_on: HAZEL (&C000-&DFFF, ACCCON Y set through play) is writable RAM, and this code only runs from there: unpack_for_play writes this code into it. &F8's value after the unpack is dead (routine header; prebuild.6502's pre_zp_list measurement). Forward reference to a '= * + 1' label is the same idiom as cm_full_below_operand in game.6502. Page crossings: the change is at the very end of hazel_b (&DDF3 on). filln moves &DE05->&DE06 and its BNE stays on page &DE. mergen_loop's BNE also stays on &DE. No hot code follows: hazel_b_end moves &DE31->&DE34, and ASSERT <= &E000 still holds. MGAME grows by 3 bytes, because music_packed follows hazel_b in the file; there are 2,271 bytes of margin under the loading picture. Window baa55fe5537a: no candidate. The only gain found was moving the zero test to bit 7 first (BPL before ASL), which would save 2 cycles per 1-byte or 3-byte run. But it needs a BEQ done added at short_or_long (line 174), which is outside the window. Doing it inside the window adds a BRA on the 01 path and on the column setup, and the net comes to about -0.1 cycles a pass, which is within the measurement's 0.1-cycle rounding, so nothing was proposed.

skeptics.reason: Not refuted. I assembled the candidate in a scratch copy. STA ucn_run_end is 8D 0B DE, and &DE0B is the operand of CPX #0 at &DE0A. skipn's LDX (AE 0B DE) and mergen_loop's CPX (EC 0B DE) read the same byte. hazel_b_end is &DE34 and the ASSERTs hold. Entries: filln, skipn, mergen and mergen_loop are referenced nowhere else in src/ or tools/, and nothing uses unpack_scenery_column+N. Each is reached only after line 216's store in the same run, so the operand always holds X+n when it is read and the initial #0 never matters. Exits: CPX #imm and CPX abs set N, Z and C as CPX zp did, and LDX abs sets N and Z as LDX zp did, so A, X, Y and every flag are the same at each exit. V comes from move_to_next_column's ADC either way, and the stack is untouched. Line 215's ADC still reads n from &F8 (line 212). The only memory difference is &F8, which now holds n instead of X+n after the walk, and that value is dead. Inside the walk, line 212 writes &F8 before every read. No other walk routine reads &F8. The code after the scroll (add_ground, edge_right/calculate_screen_addresses, add_movers, update_player's stubs) does not read it. render saves and restores &F8 through zp_save. get_mover_x_and_y and get_mover_Y_x write &F8 before check_if_mover_*_is_on_screen reads it. The prebuild path's keep_zp already gives &F8 a different value from a direct walk's. Interrupts: irq1_handler only calls sfx_tick and chains to the MOS. It never runs the walk or the prebuild and never touches &DE0B. HAZEL is writable RAM with ACCCON's Y bit set. Side effect the argument does not mention: kind-cache slot 1 starts at hazel_b_end, so KC_CAP1 goes from 231 to 230. No 12-column sprite's size on the reference disc is 230 or 231 (they run 161-257: 214, 247, 257 and so on), so the kinds that fit do not change, and the >= 214 ASSERT holds. Slot 1's arrays move by 3 bytes, which may shift a page crossing at &DF00; that changes cycles, not behaviour, and is for the gate to measure. Recount: +1 per long run (STA abs), -1 per fill iteration, +1 per skip, +1 per merge iteration. That comes to about 0.3 cycles a pass saved, and +3 bytes (the claim's -3).

The window's own count is right: STA zp->abs +1, fill CPX zp->#imm -1 an iteration, skipn LDX zp->abs +1, mergen_loop CPX zp->abs +1 an iteration; bytes +3 (STA, LDX, CPX abs; CPX # is the same 2 bytes as CPX zp), so 0.43 - 0.10 - 0.03 - ~0 = ~0.3 cycles a pass, and the opcodes, branch ranges (BNE filln/mergen_loop stay on page &DE), the forward '= * + 1' label and HAZEL being RAM are all fine. But the argument's 'no hot code follows hazel_b_end' is wrong. src/kindcache.6502 puts the kind cache's slot 1 right after it: KC_M1 = hazel_b_end, KC_CAP1 = (&E000 - KC_M1) DIV 2, KC_P1 = KC_M1 + KC_CAP1. Growing hazel_b by 3 moves KC_M1 from &DE31 to &DE34 and shrinks KC_CAP1 from 231 to 230 (KC_P1 goes from &DF18 to &DF1A). kc_draw's AND &FFFF,X (.mo, the base kc_mbl = KC_M1 - 1 + kc_off) is an indexed read on the drawing path for the helicopter bodies, which the file calls most of the bytes drawn in the late frames. Its page crossing at &DF00 moves 3 entries earlier (entry 207 to entry 204), so the number of +1 crossings in each draw of a slot-1 kind of more than 204 bytes (&45 has 214) changes by up to +3, or by a different amount if the boundary moves into another character-row group. Nobody counted that change, its sign is not known, and it is the same size as the claimed 0.3 cycles a pass. The capacity drop from 231 to 230 also means any 12-column kind of exactly 231 bytes can no longer go in slot 1, which changes the cache's behaviour. Because the net gain was not shown, this is refuted.

old:
.merge1
    STA scenery_mask
    LDA column_buffer,X
    AND scenery_mask
new:
.merge1
    AND column_buffer,X             \ grind: A = the mask, so (byte AND mask) in one (scenery_mask not written: nothing reads it)
summary: merge1 (one-byte run, non-zero mask): A already holds the mask, so AND column_buffer,X replaces STA scenery_mask / LDA column_buffer,X / AND scenery_mask. Alternative to the next candidate (overlaps it).
equivalence: merge1's only entry is BNE merge1 (local to unpack_scenery_column's scope; grep finds no other reference), with A = (mask_table_address),Y, non-zero. Old: scenery_mask := A; A := column_buffer,X AND scenery_mask. New: A := A AND column_buffer,X - the same value, N and Z from the same AND result; C and V untouched by both (C=0 as before). X, Y unchanged by both. EOR (pixel),Y then STA, INX, LDY, BRA next as before. The one difference: &A7 (scenery_mask) is not written on this path. It is scratch: merge2, merge3 and mergen each write it before reading it; no other source names &A7 (grep: zp.6502's scenery_mask only); prebuild's pre_zp_list saves and restores it around the walk and its notes measured that the logic reads none of those bytes after a walk before writing; passlock's state does not include it; the interrupt does not use it. Paging: column_buffer is &0300 main RAM in both, read with any ROMSEL/ACCCON state (old code read it too).
relies_on: A = the mask on entry to merge1 (BNE taken on it); scenery_mask dead after the column. Page crossings: column_buffer,X (&0300 + X) never crosses; (pixel_table_address),Y unchanged. Code after merge1 in hazel_b (to hazel_b_end, the last thing in the section) slides down 4 bytes: every branch from next..merge3..short_or_long stays within page ⅅ BEQ skipn still crosses (&DDF6->&DE0E, as it did &DDFA->&DE12); BNE mergen newly crosses (&DDFD->&DE13, was &DE01->&DE17), +1 cycle when taken, measured <0.017 taken a pass (STA scenery_mask at mergen 0.0 cycles) so under 0.02 cycles; filln and mergen_loop loops stay inside &DE (&DE07->&DE01, &DE26->&DE19). Nothing in main RAM moves.

skeptics.reason: Not refuted. Entry: merge1 is a local label inside unpack_scenery_column's { } scope, reached only by BNE merge1 after LDA (mask_table_address),Y (A = the non-zero mask); grep finds no other reference, no label+N, table or pushed address. Old A = column_buffer[X] AND mask, new A = mask AND column_buffer[X]: equal, N/Z from the same AND, C/V/D untouched by both, X/Y unchanged, stack untouched; flags are dead anyway (EOR, STA, INX, LDY overwrite N/Z before next reads anything). Exits identical (EOR (pixel_table_address),Y / STA / INX / LDY scenery_data_offset / BRA next). Only memory difference: &A7 not written. &A7 has one name (zp.6502 scenery_mask); only merge2/merge3/mergen use it, each STA before AND; no raw &A7 operand elsewhere (game.6502's &A7 is clouds_y_table data); prebuild's pre_zp_list saves/restores it around the walk (restore writes the saved value regardless) and the logic does not read it after a walk. irq1_handler does not touch &A7; an interrupt between instructions saves A/P, and the old code's STA..AND window on &A7 is gone, so the new code is no more exposed. column_buffer = &0300, abs,X with X 0-255 never crosses a page, main RAM readable under any ROMSEL/ACCCON as the old LDA already relied on. Recount: old STA zp 3 + LDA abs,X 4 + AND zp 3 = 10, new AND abs,X 4: 6 cycles; bytes 2+3+2 = 7 -> 3: 4 bytes. Code-slide branch-crossing effects are the machine lens's; the argument's figures there were not contradicted.

The local rewrite itself is sound on the 65SC12. AND abs,X (3D 00 03) is a real opcode at 4 cycles, and column_buffer (&0300+X) never crosses a page. Old code: STA zp (3) + LDA abs,X (4) + AND zp (3) = 10 cycles in 7 bytes. New code: 4 cycles in 3 bytes. So each execution saves 6 cycles and 4 bytes. BNE merge1 stays in range and on its page. After the shift BEQ skipn still crosses a page, BNE mergen newly crosses (+1 when taken), and the filln and mergen_loop loops stay on page &DE, all as claimed.

The argument misses something hot that sits after hazel_b. src/kindcache.6502 sets KC_M1 = hazel_b_end, so kind cache slot 1's masks start at hazel_b_end and its pixels at KC_P1 = KC_M1 + (&E000-KC_M1) DIV 2. Taking out 4 bytes moves:
- slot 1's masks from &DE31 to &DE2D
- its pixels from &DF18 to &DF16
- its capacity from 231 to 233

kc_draw reads the masks with self-modified AND &FFFF,X (kc_draw.mo). Its base is KC_M1 - 1 + kc_off for each character row, and X counts down from cnt to 1. So the move changes which mask reads pay the +1 page-crossing cycle:
- A row starting at slot index 207 or below used to cross for entries 207 and up, and now crosses only for entries 211 and up (4 fewer).
- A row starting at index 208 to 211 used to cross for none, and now crosses for entries 211 and up (a new cost).

The helicopter bodies drawn from slot 1 (&45 is 214 bytes; the bodies run 167-257) are the hottest draw in the late frames. A change of a few cycles per body draw per pass, in either direction, can be larger than the claimed 0.4 cycles a pass. Its sign depends on how the kind's bytes split into character rows at its line in the cell, and nobody has measured that. The capacity rising from 231 to 233 could also let a kind of 232-233 bytes into slot 1 where it did not fit before. That would change which slot, and which code path, draws it.

The claim says "nothing in main RAM moves" but leaves out the kind cache slot moving in HAZEL, so its cycle count is not established.

equivalence: Entry is the fall-through from STY scenery_data_offset / TAY with Y = i (1..63); skip1 is kept (BEQ skip1 still reaches INX / BRA next). Fill path (mask 0): old stored (pixel_table_address),Y; new stores (0 AND column_buffer,X) EOR pixel = pixel. Merge path (mask non-zero): old stored (column_buffer,X AND mask) EOR pixel; new the same (AND is commutative). Both then INX, LDY scenery_data_offset, BRA next as before; at next, INY and LDA set N/Z and ASL sets C before anything tests them, so the flags left differ harmlessly; A is reloaded. X and Y identical. The new read of column_buffer,X on the fill path is main RAM &0300-&03FF, harmless. scenery_mask (&A7) is no longer written by one-byte runs: dead scratch (merge2/3/n write it before reading; pre_zp_list saves/restores it; no other reader in src/). Cycles: fill old 25 (LDA 5, BNE 2, LDA 5, STA 5, INX 2, LDY 3, BRA 3), new 27 (+2, 0.12 a pass from LDA (pixel),Y's 0.6 cycles = +0.24); merge old 36 (LDA 5, BNE taken 3, STA 3, LDA 4, AND 3, EOR 5, STA 5, INX 2, LDY 3, BRA 3), new 27 (-9, 0.067 a pass = -0.6). Page crossings: (mask)/(pixel),Y as before (same pointers, same Y); column_buffer,X never crosses. Code after slides down 16 bytes to hazel_b_end: all branches between next and short_or_long stay inside page &DD (BRA next from &DD31/&DD34, BMI three to &DD4A); BEQ skipn still crosses (&DDEA->&DE02); BNE mergen newly crosses (&DDF1->&DE07), under 0.02 cycles a pass (taken <0.017 a pass); filln loop now inside &DD (&DDFB->&DDF5) and mergen_loop inside &DE (&DE1A->&DE0D), no crossing. Nothing in main RAM moves.

skeptics.reason: Equivalent on every path. The only entry is the fall-through after TAY (Y = i, 1..63); merge1 is a scope-local label with no other reference (listing: only JMP unpack_scenery_column from &1624 enters the routine), and BEQ skip1 still reaches INX/BRA next (skip1 moves &DD43->&DD44, same page). For every mask m: old stored pixel if m=0, else (buf AND m) EOR pixel; new stores (m AND buf) EOR pixel, the same value, also left in A. X, Y (reloaded from &D0) are the same; C is untouched on old and new paths (C=0 from the LSR), so C at done/move_to_next_column is the same; V and D are untouched by AND/EOR; N/Z are re-set by INY/LDA at next before any test. Stack untouched. The only memory difference is &A7 (scenery_mask), no longer written by one-byte merges: its only name is scenery_mask (zp.6502:87; no raw &A7 operand in src/, not in save_game_zp), every other reader (merge2/3/n) writes it first, irq1_handler does not touch it, pre_zp_list saves/restores it regardless. The fill path's new read of column_buffer,X (&0300 page, page-aligned, never crosses) cannot affect the result (AND 0), so an interrupt between read and write changes nothing the old code would not have. Side effect not in the argument, checked: hazel_b_end moves &DE31->&DE21, so kind cache slot 1's capacity KC_CAP1 grows 231->239 (ASSERTs still hold: &C200+239<=&C2FF, &DE21+2*239=&DFFF<=&E000); the 12-column sprite byte counts (from src/sprite_straight/andy.6502) are 257, 247, 214 and below, none in 232..239, so which kinds fit each slot is unchanged; only the slot 1 arrays' addresses move (page-crossing cycles of a few cached reads, for the gate to measure). Recount: bytes old 34, new 18 = 16 saved; fill 25->27 (+2), merge 36->27 (-9); BRA next from &DD42/&DD45 stays in page ⅅ BNE mergen newly crosses (&DDF1->&DE07, +1 when taken).

The window itself checks out on the 65SC12: every opcode is real (AND abs,X 3D, EOR (zp),Y 51, BRA 80). The new one-byte path is LDA (mask),Y 5, AND column_buffer,X 4 (column_buffer is &0300, so it never crosses a page), EOR (pixel),Y 5, STA abs,X 5, INX 2, LDY zp 3, BRA 3 = 27. The old fill path was 25 and the old merge path 36 (5+3+3+4+3+5+5+2+3+3), and the (zp),Y crossings are the same as before. Bytes: DD35-DD57 was 34, the new code is 18, so 16 are saved. The branches all stay in range, and the crossings after the change are as the argument says (BNE mergen newly crosses). The argument's own addresses are slightly off: the new BRAs to next are at DD42/DD44, not DD31/DD34. But 'Nothing in main RAM moves' misses what matters. hazel_b_end is not just the end of the copy: src/kindcache.6502 sets KC_M1 = hazel_b_end and KC_CAP1 = (&E000 - KC_M1) DIV 2, and that is where the kind cache's slot 1 sits in HAZEL. Shrinking the code by 16 moves KC_M1 from &DE31 to &DE21 and grows KC_CAP1 from 231 to 239, so KC_P1 moves from &DF18 to &DF10. Slot 1's masks move down 16 bytes and its pixels 8, and the slot holds 8 more bytes. Two effects follow, and the claim counts neither. (1) kc_draw's self-modified AND mo,X / EOR po,X reads (bases kc_mbl/kc_pbl + kc_off, X counting down) cross pages for different rows than before. Depending on kc_off a row can gain or lose crossings, at 1 cycle a byte drawn, and slot 1 is drawn hundreds of bytes a pass in the late frames. That can easily outweigh the claimed -0.36 cycles a pass. (2) kg's slot choice (kc_cap_lo/hi against kg_n) now lets 12-column kinds of 232-239 bytes into slot 1, which changes which kinds are cached and where, and so the render's timing. It also moves HAZEL workspace (the rule 'no data moves'). Not measured, so not proved no slower.

old:
.mover_is_firing_right
    LDY #&00                        \ &0008                                     # Move right a column
    JSR add_delta_to_screen_address_in_AX
    DEC projectile_x_offset
    BNE mover_is_firing_right
    BEQ subtract_y_offset           \ Always branches
new:
.mover_is_firing_right
    LDY projectile_x_offset         \ grind: right projectile_x_offset columns at once (n * 8, n <= 13:
    STA projectile_x_offset         \ MOVER_WIDEST + 2), not a column at a time; its count is dead after
    TYA
    ASL A
    ASL A
    ASL A                           \ C=0
    ADC projectile_x_offset
    BCC subtract_y_offset
    INX
    BPL subtract_y_offset
    LDX #&40                        \ round the 16K screen
    BRA subtract_y_offset           \ 65C02 opcode
summary: add_new_projectile's right-firing screen address: add projectile_x_offset * 8 in one step (n*8 <= 104, one carry, &80 wraps to &40) instead of n calls of add_delta_to_screen_address_in_AX(+&0008). Alternative to the next candidate (same lines).
equivalence: Entries: fall-through from LDY firing_direction/BMI (not taken) and BEQ mover_is_firing_right (SAM), both with A,X = the mover's screen address (high byte in &40-&7F: every writer steps it by add/subtract_delta or copies it) and projectile_x_offset = n, set this call by STX projectile_x_offset: n = 5 (SAM) or mover_types_width_table+2 <= MOVER_WIDEST+2 = 13. Old: n iterations of A+=8, X+=C, X>=&80 -> X-=&40. New: LDY n; STA lo into &88; TYA; ASL x3 (C=0, n<32); ADC lo -> lo + 8n, C its carry; INX on carry, &80 -> &40. With 8n < 256 the n steps carry at most once in total, exactly when lo+8n >= 256, so A and X agree; checked exhaustively in Python for every ring high byte, low byte and n = 1..31 (0 mismatches). Exit: every path now branches to subtract_y_offset with the same A and X (the old BEQ subtract_y_offset path). The proof depends on the firing mover's screen address high byte being in &40-&7F, and that is not guaranteed. The movers_screen_address_low/high tables (game.6502 around lines 836-844) load as all &00, and nothing initialises them, not even start_game. A slot gets a real address only when its mover touches a screen edge (calculate_screen_addresses_for_mover_on_edge, lines 1847/1849). check_if_mover_can_be_updated updates any mover up to viewport_right+&0A, which means it can move and fire there. So a newly spawned mover just past the right edge runs on its stale address. On the first game that address is &0000. move_mover_left then calls subtract_delta_from_screen_address_in_AX, and from &00xx that gives a high byte of &FF: &00-&00 with the borrow is &FF, and CMP #&40 / BCS skips the fix-up, so the address only stays in the ring if it was already >= &40. With X >= &80 the old and new code give different results, because the old add_delta subtracts &40 on every step whose high byte has N set, whether or not there was a carry. Example: &FFF0 with n=7. The old code goes &FF->&BF, &C0->&80, &80->&40 and ends at &4028. The new code carries out of lo+56, INX gives &00, BPL is taken, and it ends at &0028. With no carry at all, the old code reaches &7F after two steps while the new code leaves &FF. The projectile's movers_screen_address_high+12 is game state. The renderer passes it to world_of_address (render.6502 lines 1069-1070 and record_live 2242-2246) to place and draw the projectile, so the state, and possibly the screen, can differ from the original. The path is a never-placed slot firing right just past the right edge (for example at an ally helicopter or the tank) in the first game, which the scripted proofs are unlikely to reach. I could not show that path is unreachable, so by the rule the candidate is refuted. The other claims hold: projectile_x_offset (&88) has no alias and its exit value is dead; add_Y_rows with Y=&0A always rewrites delta_low/high; nothing enters past the label; the line is neither protected nor generated. Recount: each old iteration (LDY #, JSR, add_delta at 42 cycles, DEC zp, BNE) costs 58 cycles, so the old total is 58n+2 (466 at n=8). The new code takes 20 cycles on the BCC path, about 446 saved at n=8, as claimed. Bytes: old 11, new 19, so the code grows by 8.

So a slot still holding &0000 that moves left once (&0000 - &0008 = &FFF8) or up (rows_up keeps anything >= &40 the same way) gets a high byte of &FF/&FE/&FD. A mover can be updated, moved, turned and made to fire while up to &0A past viewport_right (check_if_mover_can_be_updated), before its edge sets its address. Enemy helicopters do exactly that: they move vertically, flip direction when no target is found, and then call consider_mover_firing_bullet. The SAM always takes this path. The dataflow annotation agrees: at entry it says X=? and after add_delta X=0..191, so the analysis does not prove X < &80 either. If that happens, the projectile's movers_screen_address_high + 12 differs. The step 2 renderer reads that through world_of_address, record_live and the rec_sh comparison, so the state and possibly the screen differ from the original's. Callers (add_player_bullet 2589 BCS, consider_mover_firing_bullet 4530 BCS via add_mover_bullet) see the same carry.
relies_on: add_new_projectile's only exit being CLC; RTS (line ~4057-4058). Slides everything from &280F to the SKIP before unused_3400_original down by 1 byte: from build/strykers.lst the only branch whose page crossing changes with -1 is BMI to_plot_mover_3055 at &2AFE (0.0 cycles a pass, stops crossing); indexed table accesses in the moved range as for the inlining candidate, all cold or stores. Independent of the inlining candidate (no overlap); together they slide +1, which changes only BCS set_frame_and_flip_3149 at &2BC4 (cold).

skeptics.reason: Entries into the changed lines: only fall-through from JSR add_new_projectile (&2807); no label sits between add_bullet and leave_with_carry_set_2b6c, and no label+N, table or numeric address references &280A-&2810 (grepped src for add_bullet/add_mover_bullet/leave_with_carry_set_2b6c offsets and literal &28xx-&33xx operands). add_new_projectile (3950-4059) has one exit, CLC; RTS at 4058-4059: all its branches stay inside (BCS/BCC use_ceiling + 2 land on STA projectiles_ttl,Y since LDA #&0E is 2 bytes), and its callees (add_delta/subtract_delta, subtract_Y_rows -> rows_up with balanced PHP/PLP or PHP/PLA, add_Y_rows) all return by RTS with the stack balanced. So C=0 after the JSR; LDX zp and INC abs,X leave C alone, so the RTS sees C=0 as before. CLC touches only C: A, X, Y, N, Z, V, D, memory and stack are identical at the RTS. An IRQ between INC and RTS saves and restores P via RTI, so it cannot change C. Callers (2589 JSR add_bullet, 4530 JSR add_mover_bullet, both BCS) see the same carry. The 1-byte slide is semantically neutral: references are symbolic, the SKIP to unused_3400_original absorbs it, ASSERT shown_screen < &3000 still holds moving down.

The semantics hold: add_new_projectile's only exit is STA projectiles_ttl,Y; CLC; RTS (both use_ceiling + 2 entries land on the STA; the four screen-address JSRs and rows_up return normally with a balanced stack), and LDX zp / INC abs,X leave C alone. So C=0 still reaches the RTS, and the removed CLC is 2 cycles and 1 byte, as claimed. The slide's page-crossing claim is wrong, though. In build/strykers.lst (the shipping build, SHIFT=0) BMI to_plot_mover_3055 is at &2AFE with offset &0C: next PC &2B00, target &2B0C, the same page, so taken costs 3. After the -1 slide it sits at &2AFD: next PC &2AFF, target &2B0B, which is across a page, so taken costs 4. The branch STARTS crossing; the argument says it stops. And it is hot, not 0.0 cycles a pass: window 678ba252a5b2 measures it at 3.0 cycles a pass, while the fall-through JSR check_if_friendly is at 0.0. That is about one taken execution a pass, so +1.0 cycle a pass against the candidate's 0.04 saved: a net loss of about 0.96 cycles a pass. Every other branch with its source or target in &280F-&3348 keeps its crossing state and stays in range (checked by script over the listing). Indexed reads with a base in the moved range can only stop crossing under a -1 shift, since no base low byte is &00, so they cost nothing. On its own this candidate makes the game slower. It would only be worth taking in a batch whose net slide leaves that BMI at &2AFE or moves it back from &2AFD, e.g. paired with the +1 inlining candidate, which the argument says changes only BCS set_frame_and_flip_3149.

LDA #&00
    STA player_y_velocity
    LDA #&28                        \ Play sound for landing
    JSR play_sound
new:
STZ player_y_velocity           \ grind: 65C02 STZ for LDA #&00 : STA
    LDA #&28                        \ Play sound for landing
    JMP play_sound                  \ grind: tail call (its RTS returns to our caller)
    SKIP 2                          \ grind: never run; keeps leave_27b8 and all after it in place
summary: end_jump (landing): STZ player_y_velocity for LDA #&00 : STA, and JMP play_sound as a tail call for JSR play_sound followed by the RTS at leave_27b8; 2 unexecuted SKIP bytes before .leave_27b8 keep it and everything after at the same addresses. 11 cycles a landing. Alternative to the next candidate (overlaps it: same JSR line).
equivalence: end_jump is entered only by BNE end_jump (line 3226; no 'end_jump +' or 'leave_27b8 +' anywhere in src/ or tools/). STZ zp stores 0 to &82 exactly as LDA #&00 : STA &82; A is then overwritten by LDA #&28, and the flags LDA #&00 set are overwritten by LDA #&28 before play_sound reads anything (play_sound reads A, sound_muted, irq_owned and its tables, not X, Y or flags on entry). Original: JSR play_sound, play_sound's RTS comes back to &23C5, whose RTS returns to this routine's caller with A, X, Y, P exactly as play_sound left them (RTS changes no register or flag). New: JMP play_sound, play_sound's RTS (or OSWORD's, via its JMP osword) returns straight to that caller with the same registers and flags. The only difference is that during play_sound the stack holds 2 bytes fewer (no return address to &23C4); play_sound and OSWORD 7 never read the stack above their own frame (no PLA/TSX of the caller's return). .leave_27b8 RTS stays at &23C5 for BEQ leave_27b8 (line 3227), which is the measured hot path (2.3 cycles a pass, all on that RTS) and is untouched. The 2 SKIP bytes at &23C3-&23C4 follow an unconditional JMP and are never executed or read.
relies_on: player_y_velocity = &82 (zero page: STZ zp, 2 bytes, 3 cycles; the LDA #&00 : STA zp pair was 4 bytes, 5 cycles). JMP abs and JSR abs are both 3 bytes, so with SKIP 2 the block is 10 bytes as before: .leave_27b8 stays at &23C5 and no code or data after it moves, so no page crossing anywhere changes (checked: a scratch build with this and the plot_character candidate differs from the control in MGAME only inside &23BC-&23C4 and plot_character's bytes plus its two JSR operands; DATA1-4, SCREEN, SRRUN identical). game.6502 is assembled CMOS (STZ is used elsewhere in it). Cycles: 2+3+2+6+6+6 = 25 -> 3+2+3+6 = 14 outside play_sound's body. Landings were not seen in the measured pass (the window's lines before the RTS show 0.0 cycles), so cycles a pass is ~0.

skeptics.reason: Not refuted. Entries: end_jump only from BNE end_jump (3226); leave_27b8 only from BEQ leave_27b8 (3227) and stays at &23C5 (set_player_y_velocity_27ac &23B9 + STX zp + RTS = &23BC; old block 2+2+2+3 = 9 bytes, new 2+2+3+SKIP 2 = 9). No label+N, address-table or tool references to end_jump/leave_27b8/&23C4 (tools key on play_sound itself, and callFrom pushes its own return). player_y_velocity = &0082 and zp.6502 is included before game.6502, so STZ zp is the 2-byte form; game.6502 already uses STZ. STZ writes the same 0 to &82; the A and N/Z that LDA #&00 left are dead (LDA #&28 overwrites both before play_sound, which reads only A, sound_muted, irq_owned and sound_data_0880). Exits: play_sound has three (RTS at leave_2f89 via BNE when muted, RTS after STA sfx_request, JMP osword whose RTS returns); in every case the old path's extra RTS at &23C5 changes no register or flag, so A, X, Y, P and memory at the routine's caller are identical, and the caller sees the same stack. Stack during play_sound is 2 bytes shallower: nothing in src reads the stack (only TXS at start-up, no TSX), irq1_handler and the MOS IRQ entry look only at their own pushed frame, and no workspace lives in page &01, so the different stale bytes below SP are never read. The ROMSEL &04 write before is unaffected. The only interrupt-visible change is that sfx_request / the OSWORD happen a few cycles earlier, a race present identically in both and not a semantic difference.

Machine lens: STZ zp (&64) and JMP abs (&4C) are real 65SC12 opcodes (game.6502 is CMOS; INC A and BRA are already used in it). Recount: old LDA# 2 + STA zp 3 + LDA# 2 + JSR 6 + play_sound's RTS 6 back to &23C5 + RTS 6 = 25 cycles; new STZ zp 3 + LDA# 2 + JMP abs 3 + play_sound's RTS 6 straight to the caller = 14 cycles, so 11 saved per landing. The block has no indexed reads or branches, so there are no page-cross terms. Bytes: &23BC-&23C4 is 9 bytes both ways (2+2+3+2 SKIP against 2+2+2+3). Built in a scratch worktree, the listing reads 23BC 64 82 / 23BE A9 28 / 23C0 4C 2A 2A / 23C3 00 00 (SKIP) / 23C5 .leave_27b8 RTS. Against a control build of HEAD, the disc differs only in MGAME's 9 bytes at &23BC-&23C4 plus the dirty-tree stamp in the catalogue, INFO and !BOOT. Nothing moves, so no page crossing or branch range changes: BNE end_jump and BEQ leave_27b8 keep their targets. No self-modifying code writes into these bytes and nothing reads them as data; the only reference to end_jump is the BNE at line 3226. play_sound (&2A2A) does not read the caller's stack frame (no TSX or PLA) on either path: the sfx50 request ends in RTS, the MOS path in JMP osword. So having 2 fewer bytes on the stack is harmless. The SKIP bytes follow an unconditional JMP and are never run.

.plot_character_row_loop
    ROL &C9

summary: plot_character's row loop as screen EOR ((screen EOR bits) AND mask): ROL; LDA (scr),Y; BCC; EOR #&3C; AND &C5; EOR (scr),Y; STA (scr),Y, dropping the LDA #0, LDA #&3C, the &C6 temp and the inverted-mask load. 32 cycles a row for 37 (clear bit), 33 for 41 (set bit): 240-384 cycles a character. 8 bytes shorter, padded by an unexecuted SKIP 8 after plot_lives's RTS so everything from the loop's end on keeps its address.
equivalence: Per row the old code stored (screen AND (mask EOR &FF)) EOR (bits AND mask), bits = &3C when the ROLled-out bit is 1, else 0 (BCC to set_pixel_value_32b8 + 2 skipped AND &C5 with A = 0, which is the same as 0 AND mask). The new stores screen EOR ((screen EOR bits) AND mask) = (screen AND NOT mask) OR (bits AND mask), the same value bit for bit (where mask is 1 it takes bits, where 0 it keeps screen; the two terms are disjoint, so EOR = OR). Both reads of (text_screen_address),Y are of the same RAM byte under the same paging (ACCCON and ROMSEL unchanged, plain RAM, no I/O; nothing else writes the text screen in between). C: ROL &C9 still takes C in from the previous row's ROL (no instruction in either loop body changes C after the ROL: LDA, EOR, AND, STA, DEY, BPL), and the first ROL's C in is unchanged, so &C9 ends with the same value. Y, X, &C5, &C8 (font_end_offset), &CE/&CF identical; A at the loop's exit is overwritten by LDA &C5 (line 4775) in both. N at the BPL comes from DEY in both. The difference is &C6, no longer written: &C6 (result_high, frames, mover_x_max_high, y, zxwrk, render's stop_y) is written before it is read on every path after plot_character: callers are only plot_text_string_loop (text_screen: completion/game over screens -> render_finish/text_screen/to_title_screen -> title_screen, whose first reads of result_high follow multiply_A_by_X_85ef's STA result_high; the title IRQ only pushes and pops it) and plot_lives, whose drawing path is dead in step 2 (BIT drawing / BPL: drawing is only ever STZ'd or restored to the game's own 0 by restore_game_zp). The game's irq1_handler and src/lib/sfx50.6502 never touch &C6. In the original the last value left there was 0 for every font character whose 6th column is 0 anyway. set_pixel_value_32b8 was referenced only by the BCC inside this loop; the new label plot_character_bit_clear is unique and keeps tools/frontend.mjs's /^plot_character/ trail filter matching. The SKIP 8 follows leave_plot_lives's RTS: no path reaches it (plot_character is entered only by JSR plot_character, lines 4739 and 4822).
relies_on: Layout (checked in a scratch build): old plot_character &2D59-&2D82 (row loop 25 bytes); new: 8 SKIP bytes &2D59-&2D60, plot_character &2D61, column loop &2D6B, row loop &2D72-&2D82 (17 bytes), so LDA &C5 (line 4775) stays at &2D83 and nothing after moves: no page crossing outside plot_character changes, and MGAME differs from the control only in these bytes, the two JSR plot_character operands and the end_jump block. skeptics.reason: Checked every path. Stored value: clear gives (S AND M) EOR S = S AND NOT M, as before (old BCC to set_pixel_value_32b8+2 stored A=0 in &C6). Set gives ((S EOR &3C) AND M) EOR S = (S AND NOT M) EOR (&3C AND M), also as before. C: nothing in either loop body touches C after the ROL. The first ROL takes C from ADC #&06 in both, later columns take it from CPX font_end_offset, so &C9 follows the same sequence. V is untouched in both. N and Z at the BPL come from DEY. A at exit is the stored byte in both and is overwritten by LDA &C5 anyway. X, Y, &C5, &C8, &CE/&CF are the same. Entries: only JSR plot_character (game.6502 4739, 4822). There are no label+N references, no references to set_pixel_value_32b8 outside the loop, no self-modification of these bytes and no absolute &2D5x-&2D8x references in src. The SKIP 8 sits after leave_plot_lives' RTS and is unreachable. Two screen reads in place of one: same byte under the same paging. The game's irq1_handler and sfx_tick never write &4000-&7FFF or &C6, and no flip is pending after render_to_main. The only difference is &C6, which is no longer written. I traced every reader. Completion text falls into game_over_screen: render_finish returns at once (shown_screen=0, flip_pending=0), and reset_screen_scroll/pre_cancel returns at once (pre_valid=0). clear_screen and convert_score_to_numbers do not touch &C6. title_screen: give_irq_back/clear_title_screen do not read it, and initialise_scrolltext_buffer's plot_title_screen_character calls multiply_A_by_X_85ef, which writes result_high before the title IRQ (push/pop only) is installed. Ground reads (result),Y only after ground_square writes result_high. plot_lives' drawing path is dead: drawing (&9B) is only STZ'd or restored from the game's own copy. Cycles recounted: old row 37 clear / 41 set, new 32 / 33. Saves 5 / 8, no page crossing (8-byte-aligned rows). Bytes: the row loop goes from 25 to 17, padded by SKIP 8, so 0 net.

Machine lens holds. Every opcode is NMOS 6502 (ROL zp, LDA/EOR/STA (zp),Y, BCC, EOR #, AND zp, DEY, BPL); no Rockwell bit ops. Recount (65SC12): old row 2+5+3+3+3+2+5+3+6+2+3 = 37 clear, 41 set; new ROL 5 + LDA (zp),Y 5 + BCC 3 + AND 3 + EOR (zp),Y 5 + STA (zp),Y 6 + DEY 2 + BPL 3 = 32 clear, 33 set (BCC untaken 2 + EOR # 2). The new loop has two (zp),Y reads where the old had one, so a page cross would cost it one more, but none can happen: every text address is 8-aligned (&4578, &5738, &4AD8, &63B8), the next-column delta for Y=0 is &08 (deltas_low_table) with a high-byte wrap of &40, so (&CE),Y for Y=0..7 stays in its page; plot_lives' drawing path is dead (BIT drawing / BPL). So 5 (clear) to 8 (set) cycles saved a row, 5 at minimum. Bytes: SKIP 8 + 17 = 25 = the old row loop, so LDA &C5 stays at &2D83 (listing: old row loop &2D6A-&2D82) and nothing from there moves; BNE plot_character_column_loop (&2D9E -> &2D6B, -&35) and BPL row loop (&2D81 -> &2D72) are in range and in page &2D; LDA font_data,X is unchanged. No self-modified operand in the range (grep: no name+N stores, set_pixel_value_32b8 referenced only by its own BCC), no code read as data there (PROTECT_BYTES covers only &0004-&001E), and plot_character is entered only by JSR at lines 4739 and 4822 (both operands assemble to the new address), so the SKIP after leave_plot_lives' RTS is never run. The interrupt between the two screen reads only writes ACCCON's D bit (line 4155), which does not change what the CPU reads; X (shadow) is unchanged. frontend.mjs's trail regex still matches the new label via ^plot_character. Executed only on the game over and completion screens: 0 cycles a pass.

BEQ done
    CMP #&80
    BEQ done
new:
BEQ done
    ASL A                           \ grind: &80 (tried, undone) to 0, as 0 is; C, Z as CMP #&80 left them
    BEQ done
summary: In pre_cancel, CMP #&80 becomes ASL A. At that point pre_valid is 1, &FF or &80, and ASL gives 0 only for &80. It is a byte shorter at the same 2 cycles. The freed byte slides edge_right down by one, so its ninth BNE * + 7 (&DBF9, taken on nearly every call) no longer crosses into page &DC.
equivalence: This line is reached only after LDA pre_valid / BEQ done is not taken, so A is 1, &FF or &80 (pre_valid's only writes are STZ, STA last_dir (1/&FF) and LDA #&80/STA). A=&80: CMP gives Z=1 C=1 N=0; ASL gives 0 with Z=1 C=1 N=0, so BEQ done is taken as before and the exit flags are identical; A leaves as 0 instead of &80. A=1: CMP gives C=0 Z=0; ASL gives 2 with C=0 Z=0, so the branch is not taken as before. N differs, but the next LDA rewrites N and Z, and C is the same. A=&FF: CMP gives C=1 Z=0; ASL gives &FE with C=1 Z=0, so the same branch and the same C. On the cancel path A is reloaded at once, and C/V pass through pre_undo (in:CV out:CV) and PLA/STA, so that exit is identical. The only difference anywhere is A = 0 instead of &80 on the &80 path. The routine's contract is 'A, X changed', and both callers write A before reading it. reset_screen_scroll runs STZ pre_valid, STZ last_dir, LDX, STX, LDY, STY, STY, DEX, STX, LDA #&08. start_clear runs STZ, STZ, PLP, JMP initialise_column_buffer, which loads X and stores with STZ; start_column's contract leaves A = 0. Neither instruction touches V, and Y is untouched. Nothing refers to pre_cancel + n (grepped). ROMSEL and its copy are untouched on the &80 path either way.
relies_on: Every path through pre_cancel takes the same cycles (CMP #imm 2, ASL A 2). The saved byte shrinks HAZEL code from &DB8F on. Of every branch from &DB87 to hazel_b_end (&DE31), only edge_right's iteration-8 BNE * + 7 changes. It goes from crossing (at &DBF9: next &DBFB, target &DC00) to not crossing (at &DBF8: next &DBFA, target &DBFF). I checked this by script over build/strykers.lst and by assembling in scratch; no branch starts crossing. The only indexed absolute read of data that moves, LDA squares,X (&DD12, X 0..3), stays in page &DD. Executions: edge_right's LDA edge_x_low costs 1005 cycles in 1500 passes on seed 1 and 834 in 600 holding RIGHT (build/grind/pc-*.json), which is 0.22 and 0.46 calls a pass. The BNE is taken unless mover 8's x low byte equals the edge's, so about 0.34 a pass averaged. hazel_b gains a byte of room. pre_cancel's &80 path ran in 2 of 30 calls in 1500 passes on seed 1; the common 0 path (24 of 30) is untouched.

skeptics.reason: Holds for every A, not only 1/&FF/&80: after BEQ done falls through A is nonzero; CMP #&80 sets Z only for A=&80 and ASL A gives 0 only for A=0 or &80, so the branch is identical for all A in 1..255; C is bit 7 of A in both; V untouched by both. N differs (bit 7 of A-&80 vs bit 6 of A) only on the fall-through, where LDA os_ram_copy rewrites N and Z at once; on the &80 exit both leave N=0. A leaves 0 instead of &80 on that exit only. Only two entries (JSR pre_cancel at &1E94 reset_screen_scroll and &2EF4 start_clear; no pre_cancel+N references in src/ or tools/), and both write A before reading it: reset_screen_scroll STZ/STZ/LDX/STX/LDY/STY/STY/DEX/STX/LDA #&08; start_clear STZ/STZ/PLP/JMP initialise_column_buffer (LDX #20, STZ loop, LDA #0). No memory, ROMSEL, stack or Y difference; the interrupt saves and restores A. Same cycles in pre_cancel (2 vs 2). Listing script over &DB87-&DE31: only edge_right's iteration-8 BNE at &DBF9 (target &DC00) changes crossing, from crossing to not; BEQ skipn at &DDFA crosses before and after; squares,X at &DCFD stays in page &DD. 1 cycle saved per taken BNE, 1 byte.

The opcode is fine: ASL A (&0A) is a real 65SC12 opcode, 2 cycles like CMP #imm, and Baron takes 'ASL A' (bank5.6502 uses it). The pre_cancel paths keep their cycles. In edge_right, iteration 8's BNE moves from &DBF9 to &DBF8 and its target from &DC00 to &DBFF, so it stops crossing a page: 1 cycle saved when taken. But the claim that 'the only indexed absolute read of data that moves is LDA squares,X' is wrong. src/kindcache.6502:45 sets KC_M1 = hazel_b_end, so slot 1's masks array starts at hazel_b_end. Removing the byte moves it from &DE31 to &DE30, and KC_CAP1 = (&E000 - KC_M1) DIV 2 grows from 231 (&E7) to 232. KC_P1 stays at &DF18. The renderer reads those masks with kc_draw's self-modified AND &FFFF,X (.mo, src/kindcache.6502:235). Its base is kc_mbl/kc_mbh + kc_off = KC_M1 - 1 + kc_off, and X counts from cnt down to 1. With the masks one byte lower, each row's base sits one byte lower against the &DF00 boundary. For example, a row at kc_off = &CF has base &DF00 now and no crossings; after the change its base is &DEFF and every one of its cnt reads takes the +1. A row one byte earlier loses one crossing. So the masks' per-read cycles change, in either direction depending on which cached kind's rows land there, and the claim neither counted nor measured this. The capacity check in kindcache_build.6502:166 also now accepts a 232-byte kind into slot 1, which changes which kinds the cache can hold. That is data moving (the grind's 'no data moves' rule) and a change in behaviour that the argument does not consider. The 1-cycle BNE saving is real, but the net count is unknown, so it is refuted.

But the 1-byte slide is not cost-neutral, and the candidate does not count it. Everything after &9C2B in bank 4 moves down 1, including sprite_straight.6502's sprite data straight_35..straight_4a (&A530-&B3xx, about 14 page boundaries). draw_column reads that data in its hottest loop, LDA (d_ptr),Y at .byte and .part_byte, plus LDA (col_ptr),Y. Moving the data down 1 is the same as moving each page boundary P up 1 relative to it. For a full cell whose d_ptr lies in (P-7, P), the cell saves 1 cycle. A cell whose d_ptr was exactly P (no crossing before) now has base P-1, so its reads at Y = 1..7 all cross: +7 cycles. Which case a column hits depends on the line, which is set by the mover's y. Ground soldiers and level-flying craft keep a fixed y, so some sprites will pay +7 per boundary column on every draw. That can outweigh the 2-cycle x 9.4-a-pass saving, and is data-dependent and unmeasured. straight_sprite_hi (&A4E4,X) also changes: X = &1C stops crossing (-1). The pixel and mask tables (&0400-&04FF, main RAM) do not move. The self-modified operands mask_operand/pix_operand(_2) are written through their labels, so the move does not break them. draw_column's own branches stay within page &9C. Measured on the bench build, pcprof seed 1, 1500 passes: interrupts 1587 -> 1360 a pass (work, the wait for the flip excluded, -53), holding RIGHT 1029 -> 965 (work -22). Bank 5 grows 15 bytes (17 free). Candidates 2-4 are subsets of this one (alternatives: they overlap).

Result = (p_hi AND 3) << 4 | p_lo >> 4 with bits 7-6 clear, which is exactly the old sequence's value ((p_lo AND &F0 OR p_hi AND &0F) rotated left 4, AND #&3F); checked for all 65,536 (p_lo, p_hi) pairs against the old ASL/ADC #&80/ROL sequence (no assumption about p_hi's range). 24 cycles, 16 bytes against 28, 21. The amplitude latch byte is (n EOR &1F) OR channel_bits with n = v >> 4 (0-15): n EOR (channel_bits OR &1F) is the same byte (channel_bits' low 5 bits are 0, n < 32), so one EOR from the table &9F, &BF, &DF, &FF (4 bytes, placed after the BRA/RTS, never executed) replaces EOR #&1F / ORA sfx_channel_bits,X in both the tone and the noise copies (-2 bytes each, +4 table: net 0). A tone channel's amplitude is sent only when it differs from the last one sent on that channel: the chip keeps its attenuation register, so the register file is the same after every tick. The last value is kept in sfx_noise_written,X for X = 0-2, bytes that nothing read before (only X = 3 holds the noise control) and that the request path already fills with the effect address's high byte (&A5-&A7, never 0-15) whenever a channel is given a new effect, so the first tick of every effect writes. A ramp change inside an effect leaves it alone (the chip still holds that amplitude); .ended / sfx_silence do not touch it but the channel is then idle (sfx_n = 0) until the next request, which re-marks it. The noise channel's own amplitude write is unchanged. Timing: the write-enable pulse stays 11+ cycles low (24 for the low byte's, 12 for the others: a longer low is harmless, the data stays on port A) and high-to-next-low is at least 20 cycles (tone low byte -> high byte: RTS, JSR, STA, STZ) against the MOS's 27+ and the chip's 16 cycles (32 clocks of 4 MHz); every other path is 32 or more. Callers other than the tone ignore A and Y on return (grep'd: sfx_tick never reads Y after sfx_output/sfx_next_ramp/.ended; the noise and .ended paths load A afresh), and the work done in the low phase for them (reading sfx_p_hi/sfx_p_lo/sfx_v at X = 0-3) has no side effects. Checked in the emulator on the bench build: the SN76489 register file (three periods, four attenuations, noise control) after every tick, 8 effects on each of 4 channels over 90 fields (32 runs), and seven scenarios (simultaneous effects, an effect replaced mid-way and by itself, sfx_silence mid-effect then a new one, noise, effects on the wrong channel, a burst of 40 requests) are identical to the control's tick by tick; the chip is written 20% fewer times (1,885 against 2,350 bytes in the 32 runs).

Not protected or generated (sfx50.6502 is hand-written; PROTECT covers only irq1_handler up to the palette writes, and sfx_tick runs after them; a shorter tick only delays the bottom split's T1 less). skeptics.reason: The code itself checks out on the 65SC12. The new high-byte sequence gives (p_hi AND 3)<<4 | p_lo>>4, 24 cycles against 28. The EOR table equals (n EOR &1F) OR channel_bits for all 4 channels. The amplitude cache is safe: request hi bytes are &A5/&A6, sfx_silence and .ended leave sfx_n=0 until a request re-marks the cache, there is no data byte without a latch, and OSWORD 7 is only reached with irq_owned clear. The next write enable falls 39 cycles or more after WE high on every path, including sfx_silence's loop at about 45. Y now leaves sfx_write as 8 instead of 0 and Z=0, but no caller reads either. The size is what fails. In the region I recount 77 -> 90 bytes, +13, because old lines 186-195 (14 bytes) stay in place unreachable. That fits the shipping build: andy_load &AFF6 + &FF9 = &BFEF leaves 17 bytes, so 4 after the change. It does not fit the gameplay disc. build/strykers-gameplay.symbols.json (built 2026-10-23 01:23 from this branch, the same time as the shipping build) has andy_load &AFFC, so bank 5 ends at &BFF5 with 11 bytes free. +13 overruns by 2, the main.6502:187 ASSERT ('bank 5 overruns its 16K') fails, and the published gameplay build no longer assembles. The gate only builds the shipping flag set, so it would not catch this. Deleting the 14 dead bytes (lines 186-195; the .noise path does not use them) would make it -1 byte and save the candidate.

Room. The candidate grows bank 5 by 13 bytes (recounted: old lines 146-185 are 63 bytes, the new text 76, and lines 186-195 stay as dead code). Bank 5's free space is the gap from andy_load + (andy_end - &8000) + PAD_END up to &C000, ASSERTed in src/main.6502. In the shipping build (build/strykers.symbols.json) andy_load is &AFF6 and andy_end &8FF9, so 17 bytes are free, as the candidate says. In the gameplay disc's build (build/strykers-gameplay.symbols.json) andy_load is &AFFC, because GAMEPLAY_* adds code to bank 5 before sfx50, so only 11 bytes are free and the gameplay build would fail the 'bank 5 overruns its 16K' ASSERT by 2 bytes. Not refuted on semantics. High byte: LDA p_hi; LSR (C=h0, A bit0=h1); EOR/AND #1/EOR p_lo (p_lo with bit0=h1); ROR; ROR (h1 h0 l7..l2); LSR; LSR = (p_hi AND 3)<<4 | p_lo>>4, the old value, bits 7-6 clear. Amplitude latch: n=v>>4 is 0-15 (sfx_v 0-&F8 by the clamps), and n EOR (bits OR &1F) = (n EOR &1F) OR bits for bits &80/&A0/&C0/&E0, so g2_att_bits (&9F,&BF,&DF,&FF) is right for tone and noise (X=3). Cache: sfx_noise_written,0-2 are written only by the request path (STA ...,X with the effect's high byte; effects are in bank 5, >= &80, never 0-15) and read only by the noise path at X=3 (grep of src and tools: no other reader or writer). sfx_n is nonzero only after a request (EQUB 0 at start, ended/sfx_silence zero it, sfx_next_ramp is reached only from the request path or a running channel), so every output on a tone channel is preceded by a request that invalidated the cache; while a channel runs nothing else writes its attenuation (no other chip writer in play: OSWORD 7 only when not irq_owned, keyboard scan uses latch line 3 and DDRA only, ended writes att 15 but zeroes sfx_n). A skipped amplitude leaves the chip's latch on the tone register, harmless because every following write is a latch byte (the only data byte is the tone high byte, always right after its latch). Exits: C and V preserved by the new sfx_write tail as by the old; the tone path's CMP changes C, but sfx_tick's next use is LDA sfx_dp / CLC on both paths. Y leaves sfx_write as 8 (was 0) and Z=0 (was 1): no caller reads either (sfx_output's caller loads A then CLC; request loop TAY; channel loop resets; sfx_silence restores P with PLP, its callers load Y (take_irq_for_play) or go through OSBYTE &13 (give_irq_back -> clear_title_screen); the irq handler PLYs). Stack balanced on every exit (g2_same RTS returns sfx_output's JSR). All runs are in the interrupt or under SEI (sfx_silence), so nothing interleaves; main code only stores sfx_request. No label+N or tool references to wait_low/wait_high/sfx_write's tail. Timing: only the 21-cycle LDY #4 wait after the write enable rises is dropped; the next fall is >= 39 cycles later on every path (noise control -> amplitude 39, tone low -> high 44, silence loop and tick paths longer), the chip needs 16. Recount (2 MHz cycles, no VIA stretch, no page crossings): each sfx_write call saves 21; a tone output saves 94 when its amplitude is unchanged (21 low write + 4 high byte arithmetic + 21 high write + 48 amplitude skipped: 25 against 73) and 58 when it changes (amplitude 61 against 73); the claim's 93 matches the unchanged case within a cycle. Bytes: 63 -> 76, +13 (the claim's -13 bytes saved), bank 5's room to be confirmed by the build's ASSERT.

Semantics hold on every path. Entries: JSR sfx_next_ramp from sfx_tick's request loop (A484-A490) and its step loop (A4DD), both inside the vsync interrupt with interrupts off; sfx_silence enters only at .ended (after SEI), which is untouched. The load reads hi*256+lo in both: old LDA &FFFF,Y with operand (lo,hi), Y=0; new LDA &FF00,Y with operand high byte hi, Y=lo; neither crosses a page (base low byte 0 / Y=0). A and N/Z come from that LDA in both, so BEQ ended takes the same branch; C and V are not touched by either sequence (LDY/LDA/STA/JSR/RTS). Y differs only before it is overwritten: on the continue path line 103 sets Y=sfx_ptr_lo in both; on the ended path sfx_write sets Y (LDY #&FF ... Y=0 at RTS) in both, so Y, A, X and flags at every exit of sfx_next_ramp are identical. Stack: the old JSR ramp/RTS pair was balanced; the new code pushes nothing; exit depth unchanged. Memory: ramp+1/ramp+2 are no longer written (they are code operands of the now-dead .ramp only); nr_c1_b0+2 is a code operand written just before use with interrupts off, in sideways RAM bank code (A4xx), so it is writable; no re-entry is possible (sfx_tick runs only in irq1_handler with I set; sfx_silence does SEI before calling .ended, and .ended does not touch the operands). Cycles: old 4+4+4+4+2+6 (JSR)+4 (LDA abs,Y, no page cross)+6 (RTS) = 34, new 4+4+4+4 = 16: 18 saved per execution, not the 20 claimed (claim overcounts by 2); about 4.0 cycles a pass at 0.22 executions, not 4.4. Not refuted on semantics; the claim's cycle figure should be corrected to 18.

.room_set
    SEC
.room_ok
    STA mark_part.base_lo           \ mark_part's base: the start - 8 (C = 1)
    ADC #3                          \ the start - 4: v_ptr, the first column's record at v_ptr + 8 (draw_column)
    STA v_ptr
    LDA #0
    LDY #7                          \ the header, at v_ptr + 4 to + 7
    STA (v_ptr),Y
    DEY

    DEY
    STA (v_ptr),Y

summary: put_on's .room: the start's high byte (the same for the start, start - 4, start - 8 and start + 1 unless the low byte borrows or carries, 9 starts in 256) is stored to all five places from one load, then the low byte makes start + 1 (INC A), start - 8 (one SEC/SBC #9 on start + 1, whose carry is also the test that no fix is needed) and start - 4 (ADC #3 on C = 1), with no reloads of v_ptr, v_ptr + 1 or the arena top. The rare starts (low byte &FF or &00-&07) take a fix block placed in the flow (BCS room_ok skips it) that DECs/INCs the high bytes already stored. 107 -> 90 cycles on the common path, 76 bytes for 72; the header-zeroing tail is unchanged (A = 0, Y = 4 at the end, as line 1382 needs).
equivalence: Outputs: save_start_lo/hi[Y], mark_part.header_lo/+1 (= start), header_hi/+1 (= start + 1), base_lo/hi (= start - 8), v_ptr/+1 (= start - 4), and the tail's A = 0, Y = 4, X unchanged (draw_mover's first act is LDX dm_slot). Checked for every low byte 0-255, every high byte 1-255 and either entry carry by a literal simulation of both sequences (identical results). Common path (low byte &08-&FE): A = low + 1 after INC A; SEC/SBC #9 gives A = low - 8 and C = 1 exactly when (low + 1) mod 256 >= 9; BCS room_ok taken; base_lo = low - 8; ADC #3 with C = 1 gives low - 4 = v_ptr's low byte; no borrow or carry reaches the high byte (low >= 8 so start - 4 and start - 8 do not borrow; low <= &FE so start + 1 does not carry), so the plain high byte stored to v_ptr + 1, base_hi and header_hi + 1 is right. Rare path (C = 0; A = low - 8 mod 256 = &F7 for low &FF, &F8-&FF for low 0-7): CMP #&FC / BCS room_base for low 4-7 (only start - 8 borrows: DEC base_hi); else CMP #&F8 / BCC room_carry for A = &F7 (low &FF: INC header_hi + 1, start - 4 and start - 8 do not borrow); else low 0-3 (start - 4 and start - 8 both borrow: DEC v_ptr + 1 and DEC base_hi). Every rare exit does SEC and falls into room_ok with A still = low - 8, so STA base_lo / ADC #3 / STA v_ptr give the same low bytes. The original's own assumption (C = 1 after the high-byte SBC #0, i.e. the arena's high byte >= 1; it is &30-&3F) is the one the new code needs (DEC of a stored high byte >= 1). A passlock of the change (scratch copy, control = HEAD build, seed 1, 2,500 passes, --screen --unclobber): state and screen identical every pass. The changed order of the stores (v_ptr + 1 before v_ptr, the operands before the low bytes) is invisible: nothing in an interrupt reads v_ptr (&C4/&C5), save_start_* or mark_part's operands, and mark_part is not run between the window's first and last store.

summary: R-first clip: compute right - x once (the viewport is always 79 columns wide), test R in 0..78 with four not-taken branches, store jmin 0 / jmax R and go straight to jmax_done; the rare left-of-view case (6% of calls) recomputes left - x and re-enters left_of_view with jmax already set (jmin_done is just BRA jmax_done). Alternative to the other candidate (same lines).
equivalence: R = right - x (16-bit exact). Original: chain C = (R >= 0); R high byte zero => jmax = R low else 255; D = left - x >= 0 => left_of_view (jmin = D low if D high 0 else 255) else jmin 0. Invariant right = left + 79 gives D = R - 79. New: BCC <=> R < 0 -> falls out of the window to the same SEC (SKY_MODE) / RTS as before (dm_jmin/dm_jmax are not read after that exit: sky_put_on branches to fall on C, draw_mover returns). BNE with C = 1: R >= 256, so D >= 0 and the original stores jmax 255 and calls left_of_view; new stores 255 (LDY #&FF / STY), recomputes D with the original chain so C = 1 and Z = (D high is 0) on entry to left_of_view exactly as before, BRA left_of_view, which sets dm_jmin and returns via BRA jmin_done -> BRA jmax_done. H = 0 and Y >= 79: R = 79..255, D >= 0, jmax = R low = Y (high byte zero so no clamp), same recompute path. H = 0 and Y < 79: R = 0..78, D < 0: original takes the fall-through (jmin 0), jmax = R low (high zero so not_right_of_view does not clamp); new STZ dm_jmin / STY dm_jmax / BRA jmax_done. A is dead at jmax_done (LDA dm_typecol), Y is reloaded there, X = slot kept, flags dead. Hot path 46 -> 35 cycles to jmax_done (the old count includes not_right_of_view's taken BEQ jmax_done); rare path about 6 cycles more.

Y is dead at every exit (the draw_mover caller at render.6502 1383 then LDY dm_index; sky.6502's dm_setup caller reloads before use; the code after jmax_done sets Y). jmin_done is only entered by left_of_view's BRA. skeptics.reason: The opcodes, branch ranges and counts check out on the 65SC12: hot path 46 -> 35 cycles (11 saved), 30 -> 45 bytes (+15). The equivalence is still wrong. It assumes that right = left + 79 (mod 65536) makes D = left - x equal R - 79 with the same unsigned borrows. That fails whenever the 16-bit viewport wraps: left is &FFxx while right is &00xx. The game starts that way: reset_screen_scroll sets left &FFB0, right &FFFF, and the first right scroll makes right &0000 while left is still &FFB1. Observer mode (game.6502 observer_mode_loop) scrolls LEFT from column 0 with no bound, and each step renders (update_screen_observer -> update_screen). One LEFT from the start gives left = &FFFF, right = &004E. Take a mover at x = &0010. The old code finds left >= x unsigned, goes to left_of_view, D = &FFEF, high byte non-zero, so jmin = 255 (nothing visible): it is clipped. The new code finds R = &3E with no borrow, high byte 0 and Y < 79, so it stores jmin 0 and jmax &3E and draws the mover. So draw_mover behaves differently in a state the shipping build can reach (tools/observer.mjs drives LEFT). The window also grows 15 bytes and slides bank 4's later indexed table reads, which the candidate does not count.

The candidate relies on the viewport never wrapping, so that the unsigned borrow of left - x always equals R >= 79. That is false. reset_screen_scroll (game.6502 ~2615) sets left = &FFB0 and right = &FFFF (Y = &FF after DEY into left_high and right_high), not &00B0/&00FF as relies_on says. Scrolling past a 16-bit boundary leaves right < left unsigned. Observer mode's LEFT has no limit (observer_mode_loop -> scroll_screen_left -> update_screen_observer -> update_screen -> render -> draw_mover). One LEFT from the start view (left &0000, right &004F) gives left &FFFF, right &004E. For a mover at x = &0010 the old code takes the left - x path with no borrow (&FFEF) into left_of_view with high byte &FF, so jmin = 255 and jmax = &3E: nothing is drawn. The new code sees R = &3E < 79 and sets jmin 0, jmax &3E, so the mover is drawn. dm_jmin differs and the screen differs on a path the scripted proofs barely reach (observer mode; tools/observer.mjs, BUGS #11). The width-79 invariant holds only modulo 65536, and the candidate's carry argument needs it unsigned. Also unchecked: bank 4 code after draw_mover grows by 15 bytes, which moves the page phase of the indexed tables (acknowledged as not counted).

Checked every entry and exit. Entries: dm_setup/draw_mover fall-through (sky.6502 JSR draw_mover.dm_setup, put_on's JSR draw_mover), jmin_done only from left_of_view's BRA, left_of_view only from this block, not_right_of_view becomes dead. Exits: (1) R<0 -> g3_far -> [SEC] RTS: A, N, Z, C, V identical to the old exit (both from SBC movers_x_high); Y now = R low (was caller's Y) but dead: non-sky caller does LDX back/LDY dm_index, sky caller goes to fall (sky_erase_old -> sky_old_geom -> sky_geom TAY first) or put_on .room LDY dm_index; dm_jmin/dm_jmax not written on this exit but only read in draw_mover's body and sky.6502 after a C-clear dm_setup. (2) R 0..78 -> jmin 0, jmax R, BRA jmax_done (LDY #, LDA dm_typecol: A, Y, flags dead). (3) R>=79 -> jmax R low or 255, D recomputed by the original chain so left_of_view sees the same C=1/Z and its jmin_low SBC the same carry. The equivalence needs right = left+79 with no 16-bit wrap. NOTE the relies_on is factually wrong about the start: reset_screen_scroll sets left &FFB0 / right &FFFF (not &00B0/&00FF), so wrapped states (left &FFB1..&FFFF, right &0000..&004E) exist during scroll_into_world and in observer mode after LEFT from the world start (unguarded). In such states the new code would give jmin 0 where the old gives 255 for x in 0..R. But draw_mover is unreachable there: put_on/sky_put_on run only with need bit 6, set only by mark_to_draw's check_if_mover_is_on_screen, which in a wrapped view rejects every mover (x_high 0: Y - left_high &FF borrows; x_high >= &80 means an empty slot), and shown-and-staying records are not redrawn; scroll_into_world renders nothing (update_screen_without_delay, render_start after). Elsewhere all writers keep the pair consistent: scroll_screen_left/right move both 16-bit, view_to_buffer/buffer_to_view/history_to_view copy snapshots taken together (history_push after the scroll), prebuild shifts and restores both low bytes inside its routine, restore_game_zp does not write them, shield rewind uses scroll_screen_left and stops at left 0. IRQ does not read or write dm_* or the viewport; no stack change. Recount: old hot path to jmax_done 46 cycles (3+2+4+3+4+2+3+3+2+4+3+3+4+3+3), new 35 (3+2+4+2+3+4+2+2+2+2+3+3+3): 11 saved, page crossings aside; R<0 path 42 -> 21; left-of-view path slower. Bytes: old 30, new 45: +15 (claim -15 = 15 bytes larger).

Self-modifying code: none touches this region. vertical_rows_jsr_b245f+1 patches only the caller's JSR low byte, and ru_lo/ru_d/unused_0076 are read only inside rows_up and add_Y_rows. bank5's unused_0076+1 is &77, and neither the IRQ nor the renderer reads &76. On the crossing path ru_lo is no longer written, but it is read nowhere after this point, and every call re-stores it at entry, so a Y>=8 read of ru_cells_hi+8 (=ru_lo) would still see the same byte. The single ORA #&40 wrap equals the two CMP/ADC wraps whenever X is &40-&7F and Y<=7: v1 is &2E-&7F and t is &2B-&7F, checked case by case. The arithmetic fails for X>=&80 or X=&00-&02 edge cases (for example X=0 with an initial zero mover address). So I probed the base ship build, the whole world from a cold first game with the WorldBot: 11,412 passes to completion, 28,285 rows_up calls, 26,399 on the crossing path. Every X was in &40-&7F, the largest Y was 4, and none were out of range. C and V on exit change. Callers: plot_mover_sprite/walk_column CLC before using C; move_mover_right/left CLC/SEC; the projectile path through add_Y_rows reaches CPX #&05 before any flag read. No BVC/BVS follows. A, X, Y and unused_0076=0 on exit are unchanged.

The single ORA #&40 wrap is only equal to the original's two CMP/ADC wraps if X (the address high byte) is in &40-&7F on entry, and that is not true on every path. movers_screen_address_low/high are zero-initialised tables (src/game.6502 836-842) and are written only by calculate_screen_addresses_for_mover_on_edge (1847), the move (2977), use_player_position (3013), projectiles (4225) and the shield's rewind. The first helicopter in each slot after boot therefore moves with movers_screen_address_high = &00. A move up toward an airborne target (y_delta 1-3 rows, AND #&83) goes check_for_collision_after_vertical_move -> subtract_Y_rows_from_screen_address_in_AX with A = &00, X = &00. Then line = 0, so it takes the crossing path: Y = 0, L1 = 0, no borrow, v1 = 0. The original wraps that to &40, CPY #&80 gives C = 0, SBC #2 gives &3D, which wraps to X = &7D. Behaviour: act is appended only at .listed in the classify loop with X ascending 0..MOVER_SLOTS-1, each slot once, and gather walks act in order appending list_slot at list_n, so list_slot is strictly ascending, slot 0 only at entry 0: 'slot b < slot a' == 'entry b < entry a', and the player's 'every other b' is the full sweep (its own entry has need 0, skipped). list_overlap is symmetric and keeps X and Y; it returns C clear on 'no'. C is clear at .each_a's fall-through (CPX list_n with X < list_n) and untouched on the way to c1_done, so BCC next_a after LDX list_b is right on every no-overlap path. Marks only go 0 -> &C0 and the sweep repeats to a fixpoint, so visiting b in another order gives the same final need[] (only the sweep count may differ, which affects nothing but cycles). No raster-timed code; render is not on the front end, title, define controls or completion paths beyond what render_pass already drives, and the predicate is the same on every list. Branch ranges fine (BNE gather+4 offset -&37; BEQ swept, BCC next_a reach). Recount: tail saves 2 cycles a gather iteration (5 on the last); a staying-b iteration 29 -> 16 by my count (LDY abs,X 4, LDA abs,Y 4, BEQ taken 3, DEX 2, BPL 3), close to the claim; other flag builds may lay the loop across a page differently, which costs cycles only.

Checked every path. Tail: act_n is zero page (&4F), so gather's CPY act_n + BEQ gathered is 4 bytes and gather + 4 is STY ren_k (the local gather, not compact's, which is in its own scope); Y = ren_k+1 <= act_n so on the BNE path Y < act_n and C = 0, as gather's CPY left it for the TXA/ADC boff; equal falls into .gathered as gather's BEQ did. Sweep: act is written only at render.6502 .listed in the classify loop (X ascending 0..MOVER_SLOTS-1), gather walks act in order, so list_slot is strictly ascending, slot 0 only at entry 0; 'b slot < a slot' is 'b entry < a entry', and for the player every other entry, entry 0 itself skipped by need = 0. b with slot 0 skipped by TYA/BEQ as before. need is not written while a is examined, so 'any b overlaps' is the same predicate whatever the visit order: each sweep marks the same set, not merely the same fixpoint. C into .c1_done: CPX list_n with X < list_n gives C = 0, nothing up to the BMI or in the loop body touches C, list_overlap returns C = 0 for no and does not touch X, Y or need; BCS only on overlap. list_n <= MOVER_SLOTS = 34, so DEX/BMI/BPL are sound. After .c1_done X = a's entry for INX at next_a and for the marking path's LDY list_slot,X; STA list_changed / BRA next_a follow unchanged with A = &C0. At RTS: X = list_n and A = 0 as before, Y and list_b differ: the caller does LDX #0 / JSR take_off (which sets Y itself); list_b (&6E, the only symbol there) is read nowhere else; no label in the replaced span is referenced from outside the scope (.below gone, .next_b now dead but harmless). Stack: one balanced JSR. The interrupt reads none of need, list_*, ren_k, act_n, and no new memory is written. Bytes recounted 68 old, 68 new (abs,Y for need,Y as need has no zp,Y LDA/STA), so 0 and nothing after moves. Cycles: a staying b costs 16 statically (LDY abs,X 4, LDA abs,Y 4, BEQ 3, DEX 2, BPL 3) against 29, and only entries before a are visited; the tail saves 2 per gather iteration; the 14.2 a call is the measurement, not recounted here.

Same bytes (45) as the old LDY #0 .. STA need,Y, so nothing after the window moves. Overlaps the first candidate (alternative: use this one if the C-flag exit or gather + 4 is refused). Measured with pcprof on the unshifted DEBUG_LIVES build, 1500 passes seed 1: render 23430 -> 23401 a pass; holding RIGHT 28406 -> 28369.

Same predicate, same pairs, b in descending entry order (marks monotone, the sweep repeats to the same fixpoint); with list_slot strictly ascending, slot b < slot a is entry b < entry a and slot a = 0 is entry 0 (b over all others, via LDX list_n / DEX). JSR list_overlap gets X = b entry, Y = a entry (symmetric, keeps both). Nothing live after RTS. Verified by the same JS-port fuzz: 8,020 sweeps, 0 mismatches (1,638 marking).
