The outside .next_b (LDY list_b / INY / BRA each_b) becomes unreferenced dead code (5 bytes; outside the window so it stays) and each_b must stay defined for it. Page crossings: 45 bytes before and after (LDY #0 .. STA need,Y), every later address unchanged (checked: list_recorded &9862, widen_by_live &98EE, bench and ship builds); no branch in the replaced code crosses a page (all within &9800-&98FF) and the tail's BRA gather is untouched (still 4 cycles).

skeptics.reason: Machine lens: every opcode is valid on the 65SC12 (STX zp, TYA, BNE/BMI/BEQ/BCS/BPL, LDX zp, DEX, LDY abs,X, LDA abs,Y, JSR, BRA; no Rockwell bit ops). Bytes recounted: new is 2+1+2+2+1+2+3+3+2+1+2+2+3+2+1+2+2+2+2+3+2+3 = 45, old &9824-&9850 = 45, so STA list_changed stays at &9851 and nothing after it moves. All branches stay inside page &98, short range (each_b moves to &982E; the now-dead .next_b's BRA each_b is -&2C, still in range; c2_done's BRA next_a reaches &985A). Indexed reads: list_slot &B780+X and need &001F+Y (abs,Y) with entries/slots < MOVER_SLOTS never cross a page. list_overlap is symmetric (x2[Y]>=x1[X], x2[X]>=x1[Y], y2[Y]>=y1[X], y2[X]>=y1[Y]), keeps X and Y, and its tables (&B7A3, &B7C6, &BE80, &BEA3, &BEC6, &B8C8) do not cross pages for those indices whichever register indexes them, so the swap costs nothing. No self-modifying operand or data read in &9824-&9851 (no label+1 stores into close_over_overlaps). Entry state: Y = a's slot and A = need = 0 from the fall-through, so TYA/BNE picks the player correctly; act is appended with X ascending in classify (render.6502 .listed) and gather keeps order, so entries are slot-ordered and slot 0 can only be entry 0. Recount: a staying b costs old 29 (CPY 3, BEQ 2, STY 3, LDA abs,Y 4, TAY 2, LDA abs,Y 4, BEQ 3, LDY 3, INY 2, BRA 3), new 16 not the 15 the summary says (LDY abs,X 4, LDA abs,Y 4, BEQ 3, DEX 2, BPL 3); fixed costs a staying a: old 2 + exit 6; new 12-13 setup + 10 exit (LDX/BRA added), but b now runs only over entries before a, so the measured 58 a call / 29 a pass is plausible; the one-cycle slip in the narrative does not change the saving's sign.

Project lens: no PROTECTED line, generated source, table or raster-timed code; runs in close_over_overlaps (bank 4, called once from render with the same paging as before), reads and writes the same RAM (need zp &1F+, list_slot in bank 4 workspace, list_n &53, list_changed) plus list_b (&6E), which is renderer-only scratch in ren_zp (no alias in zp.6502 or elsewhere; only this routine touches it) and is dead after return, so leaving a's entry there instead of b's changes nothing. act is built in ascending slot order by classify (X 0..MOVER_SLOTS-1) and gather lists a subset in act order, so list_slot is strictly ascending and slot 0 can only be entry 0: 'b drawn before a' = 'entry before a', and the player (Y=a's slot=0 at TYA, Y still holding list_slot,X from the LDA need,Y check) searches all entries via LDX list_n. b's need/TYA skips match the old (b staying, b the player; b=a has need 0). The mark is on a only and need of b is not changed during a's b-scan, so scanning b descending marks exactly the same a's within each sweep: same need[], same list_changed, same fixpoint, same draws. list_overlap keeps X and Y (only A and C touched). Both exits restore X = a's entry (LDX list_b) before next_a / the outside STA list_changed. Bytes recounted 45 = 45 (need and list_slot indexed by Y are absolute,Y 3 bytes in both), so nothing after moves; old .next_b becomes unreachable but still assembles against the kept .each_b label. DEX/BMI safe (list_n <= MOVER_SLOTS < 128). Cycle recount: a staying b costs 16 in the new loop (LDY abs,X 4, LDA abs,Y 4, BEQ taken 3, DEX 2, BPL taken 3), not 15, against 29 in the old; b's after a are no longer visited at all. Claim per pass rests on the pcprof measurement; I cannot verify its 58 per execution exactly but the direction and size are plausible.

Checked every path. Entry: only fall-through from BNE next_a (line 1099) with Y = a's slot (LDY list_slot,X; LDA need,Y leaves Y), so TYA/BNE splits player and mover correctly. act is written only at render.6502 .listed (STA act,Y in classify, X rising 0..MOVER_SLOTS-1) and gather walks act in order, so list_slot is strictly ascending: 'b slot < a slot' is 'b entry < a entry', and slot 0 can only be entry 0. Mover a: old tests b with 0 < slot b < slot a; new tests entries X-1..0, skipping slot 0 with TYA/BEQ: the same set. Player a: old tests every b with slot != 0 (CMP list_slot,X = 0 gives C set, LDY list_slot,X = 0 falls to .below); new tests every entry (LDX list_n), slot 0 skipped: the same set, wherever the player sits. a itself is skipped in both by need = 0. Same predicate (list_overlap is symmetric under swapping X and Y, keeps both, writes only A and flags), only the search order differs, and the result per a (marked or not) does not depend on order, so the sweep's state changes exactly as before, a by a. Exits: c2_done and c2_mark both restore X = a's entry from list_b; c2_mark falls into STA list_changed with A = &C0 then BRA next_a as before; next_a reads only X (INX, CPX), so the different A, Y, list_b and flags at exit are dead (swept reloads A; list_b is only in this routine and written before any read, both versions). list_n <= MOVER_SLOTS = 34 < 128, so DEX/BMI and DEX/BPL are sound, and a mover at entry 0 exits at once (DEX to &FF) as old found no lower slot. Stack balanced (one JSR/RTS). Interrupts: list_b and need are the renderer's zero page, held across JSR list_overlap in both versions; no new exposure. Dead .next_b (BRA each_b) is unreachable; each_b stays defined; .below had no other referrer. Bytes: 45 old, 45 new (counted opcode by opcode against build/strykers.lst &9824-&9850, list_slot &B780 absolute, need,Y absolute,Y), so nothing after moves; all of it in page &98, list_slot+X and need+Y never cross a page. Cycle quibble only: a staying b costs 16 new (LDY abs,X 4, LDA abs,Y 4, BEQ 3, DEX 2, BPL 3), not the 15 the summary says, vs 29 old; the per-pass figure is the optimiser's pcprof measurement and also includes the shorter b range for movers, so I keep its 58 per execution as unrefuted but not independently recounted.

    SBC #2
    BCC lrec_low

    LDA list_x_hi
    ADC #0
    STA list_x2_hi,Y

summary: search_for_target's mover loop: (1) the prefilter runs with X = mover - 1 so its end test is the DEX's own Z flag (DEX/BEQ, 4 cycles) instead of DEX/CPX #2/BCC (6) on each of the ~20 passed-over movers a pass, mover 1 branching to an INX in front of the full check; (2) set_cm_left is inlined with its two results stored straight into the left test's CMP #/SBC # operands (saves the JSR/RTS and 4 cycles on each of ~4 left tests a pass); (3) the entry search_for_target_loop is just BEQ (every way there is right after a DEX), 2 bytes and 2 cycles less; (4) the loop is put on a page boundary (never-run pad in front of it) so none of its hot branches crosses a page (the old loop had the BPL back, the BCC to the full check and the skip BCC crossing &27xx/&28xx). Wrapped in IF SKY_MODE: the SKY_MODE=0 builds (the DEBUG_FULLREDRAW oracle, SKY_HELI=0) keep the original code, since they have only 9 bytes free in the main block and this grows it by 28. Measured on the bench build (pcprof, 2026-10-22): work a pass seed 1 34457 -> 34381 (logic 9440 -> 9349), RIGHT 39690 -> 39594 (logic 10255 -> 10155). passlock seed 1 3000 passes and seed 3 2000 passes with screen, oracle (DEBUG_FULLREDRAW) seed 5 2500 passes with screen, and helilock flight 5: identical. Best of three (the others overlap it: alternatives).
equivalence: The prefilter visits the same movers in the same order with the same tests: mover X (11 down to 2) is passed over by the same right-of-range and left-of-range comparisons on the same data, and movers 1 and 0 are always checked in full. Biased index: inside the prefilter X holds (mover - 1) and every table read is base + 1,X, so the DEX/BEQ pair does the work of DEX/CPX #2/BCC: X reaches 0 exactly when the next mover is 1, and the BEQ target INX restores X = 1 for the full check. A mover that passes the prefilter reaches the JSR through INX, so check_for_mover_collision_with_mover_X, the BCS and consider_next_enemy see X = the mover as before. A at each JSR is the same: the same LDA/CMP/LDA/SBC sequence leaves it (INX/DEX/BEQ do not touch A or C), and Y is never touched. Left bound: the inlined set_cm_left is the same instruction sequence (LDA mover_x_low, SEC, SBC #MOVER_WIDEST, low byte; LDA &C5; no borrow keeps &C5; a borrow does SBC #0, and INC A when that borrows again: &FF -> 0, low byte 0) with the stores going to the CMP #/SBC # operand bytes instead of cm_left_low/cm_left_high; the borrow case is moved out of line behind the BRA and rejoins with the same A. The left test then compares with the same two bytes. Nothing else reads cm_left_low/cm_left_high after search_for_target without first calling set_cm_left (grep: the range loop at 3532 and the friends loop at 3967 each call it before reading; the tools do not read them). Entry: search_for_target_loop is entered only by consider_next_enemy's DEX/BPL and found_target_2b1f's DEX/BPL (grep search_for_target_loop: lines 4047 and 4079 only), both right after a DEX with X >= 0, so Z = 1 iff X = 0 (the full check of mover 0); X = 1 goes through the prefilter's DEX to X = 0 and the BEQ to INX, a full check of mover 1; X >= 2 tests mover X. The first entry from the setup is LDX #&0A / BRA into the first test (mover 11). Exit: search_done unchanged (reached by fall-through when the BPL is not taken). The V flag is set by the same SBC/ADC operands as before. The IF SKY_MODE ELSE branch is the original text, so the SKY_MODE=0 builds are byte-for-byte what they were.
relies_on: Page crossings: after the change the loop (BEQ entry, DEX/BEQ head, tests, INX, JSR, BCS, DEX, BPL: &2800-&2829 in the bench build) lies wholly in page &28; the old code's crossing taken branches (BPL back, BCC to search_in_full, the skip BCC at the left test, each +1 cycle: about 10 a pass) are gone, and the move of everything after search_done by 28 bytes is inside the measured totals. Needs the pad in front of the loop: IF LO(*) >= &E0 / SKIP &100 - LO(*) puts the loop on the next page boundary when the code before it ends in the last &20 bytes of a page (it ends at &27FB in the bench, ship and release builds: pad 5); if earlier edits move that code the loop stays aligned or, outside the last &20 bytes, merely unaligned (slower, still correct). Branch range: search_done must stay within 128 bytes of check_if_friendly for the BPL right after it (line 4049 + 1): with the loop at &2800 it is exactly -128 (BPL at &282C -> &27AE); no more bytes can be added to the window. Room: +28 bytes in the main block (SKY_MODE=1 only; 193 free before, 165 after); the IF SKY_MODE wrapper keeps the DEBUG_FULLREDRAW and SKY_HELI=0 builds as they were. Assembled in bench, full, ship, release, gameplay, SKY_HELI=0 and SKY_HELI=2. Self-modifying operands: stf_left_low_operand_ve / stf_left_high_operand_ve are the CMP #/SBC # operands written at the start of each search (main RAM below &3000, the way stf_x_max_high_operand_s already is). No JSR name+N or other entries past a changed label (grep search_for_target_loop, search_prefilter_next, search_in_full, stf_left_test_s, consider_next_enemy: only inside this region and the two DEX/BPLs above). New labels carry the _ve suffix.

Project lens, checked by applying it in a scratch worktree and building ship, release, bench (-Define DEBUG_LIVES), full (DEBUG_LIVES,DEBUG_FULLREDRAW), gameplay, gameplay release, SKY_HELI=2 and SKY_HELI=0: all assemble. Room: the main block's free space before &3400 goes 193 -> 165 in ship and bench, as claimed. The SKY_MODE=0 builds (the oracle, SKY_HELI=0) take the ELSE branch, which is the old text verbatim. No PROTECTED line, generated source, table or raster-timed code is touched. Memory: cm_left_low/high are no longer written by search_for_target; their only other readers (the range search at 3549/3551, the friends search at 3978/3980) each call set_cm_left first and cannot be entered past it, and check_for_mover_collision_with_mover_X/check_for_collision_with_mover/check_if_friendly, called inside the loop, neither read nor write them, so the old code's left test always read the values set at the search's start, which the new immediates hold. The two new self-modified operands are in main RAM below &3000 (code at &27xx-&28xx), so ACCCON's X bit and ROMSEL/ANDY do not matter. No harness reads the changed labels; tools/pccats.py only uses the names to group profile categories, so the new _ve labels would be counted outside 'collide' (cosmetic). Behaviour: movers 11..2 get the same prefilter tests on the same bytes (base+1,X with X = mover-1), movers 1 and 0 are always checked in full, both ways into search_for_target_loop (consider_next_enemy's and found_target_2b1f's) are DEX/BPL so its BEQ sees the DEX's Z, and A, X, Y, C and V at every JSR and at exit match. The inlined set_cm_left computes the same two bytes, including the borrow and below-0 cases. Cycles: -2 on each passed-over mover, -4 on each left test, about -11 per search for the JSR/RTS, but +2 on each full check of a mover >= 3 followed by a prefilter test (BEQ/DEX/BEQ instead of CPX/BCC); net per pass is the measurement's, which is plausible at ~76.

Every path checked. Entries: search_for_target is reached only by JSR from 4536/4543/4585 and through search_for_target_with_offset (4718/4730), and the prefix up to STX target is unchanged. search_for_target_loop is entered only from consider_next_enemy's DEX/BPL and found_target_2b1f's STX/DEX/BPL (grep src and tools: no other references, no label+N), so Z there is the DEX's own (Z=1 iff X=0). consider_next_enemy is still entered from check_if_target_is_better's BPL at its DEX. The other changed labels (search_prefilter_next, stf_left_test_s, search_in_full) are referenced only inside the region. Index bias: with X'=mover-1, base+1,X reads the same bytes. Passed-over mover m>=3 leads to DEX then test of m-1. Mover 2 passed over: DEX gives X'=0, BEQ to INX, full check of mover 1. Loop entry X=1: DEX/BEQ/INX, full check of 1. X=0: BEQ, full check of 0. First test: LDX #&0A/BRA tests mover 11, as LDX #&0C/DEX/CPX did. Registers at the JSR: check_for_mover_collision_with_mover_X begins CPX/BEQ (CLC RTS) or get_mover_X_type_and_height, which loads A and Y before reading them. A, Y and C on entry are dead, so the one difference (old C=0 from CPX #2 for movers 0 and 1; new C can be 1 after a friendly found_target_2b1f) is harmless. V is never read (no BVC/BVS/CLV in game.6502); D is clear in play. The inlined set_cm_left is the same sequence, borrow and double-borrow included (INC A gives 0 into both operands), so CMP #/SBC # see the same bytes and leave the same A and C as CMP abs/SBC abs. cm_left_low/high are no longer written by this search. Their only readers (the range loop at 3532 and the friends loop at 3967) each JSR set_cm_left first, and no tool reads them. Exit: search_done is reached as before with X=&FF and the same N. A and Y at the exit come from the same full checks of movers 1 and 0. Stack: JSR/RTS removed as a pair; BRAs only. Pad: placed after an unconditional BRA, never executed. Interrupts: the operands are main RAM below &3000, and irq1_handler touches neither they nor movers_x tables. SKY_MODE=0 builds take the ELSE branch, the original text. Recount: a passed-over mover costs 2 cycles less (DEX/BEQ instead of DEX/CPX/BCC). Each left test costs 4 less (immediates). Per search, the JSR/RTS of set_cm_left goes (minus the BRA). Page-crossing gains are the machine lens's to check. Bytes: the old region is 48 and the new one 71 plus a 5-byte pad (bench), so the code grows by 28, as claimed.

summary: Alternative to the first (overlaps it), without the BEQ-only entry: the loop entry keeps CPX #2 / BCC search_in_full, so it does not depend on the Z of the DEX before it. equivalence: The prefilter visits the same movers in the same order with the same tests: mover X (11 down to 2) is passed over by the same right-of-range and left-of-range comparisons on the same data, and movers 1 and 0 are always checked in full. Biased index: inside the prefilter X holds (mover - 1) and every table read is base + 1,X, so the DEX/BEQ pair does the work of DEX/CPX #2/BCC: X reaches 0 exactly when the next mover is 1, and the BEQ target INX restores X = 1 for the full check. A mover that passes the prefilter reaches the JSR through INX, so check_for_mover_collision_with_mover_X, the BCS and consider_next_enemy see X = the mover as before. A at each JSR is the same: the same LDA/CMP/LDA/SBC sequence leaves it (INX/DEX/BEQ do not touch A or C), and Y is never touched. Left bound: the inlined set_cm_left is the same instruction sequence (LDA mover_x_low, SEC, SBC #MOVER_WIDEST, low byte; LDA &C5; no borrow keeps &C5; a borrow does SBC #0, and INC A when that borrows again: &FF -> 0, low byte 0) with the stores going to the CMP #/SBC # operand bytes instead of cm_left_low/cm_left_high; the borrow case is moved out of line behind the BRA and rejoins with the same A. The left test then compares with the same two bytes. Nothing else reads cm_left_low/cm_left_high after search_for_target without first calling set_cm_left (grep: the range loop at 3532 and the friends loop at 3967 each call it before reading; the tools do not read them). Entry: the entry keeps CPX #2 / BCC search_in_full, which sends X < 2 straight to the full check as the original did, so there is no assumption on the flags at the entry; X >= 2 falls into the prefilter's DEX and tests mover X. The first entry from the setup is LDX #&0A / BRA into the first test (mover 11).
relies_on: Page crossings: the DEX and everything after it are in page &28; the entry CPX/BCC (&27FC) is in page &27, so the BPL back to it crosses (+1 cycle, about 5 a pass) and is the only hot crossing left. Branch range: search_done at &2828, BPL check_if_friendly displacement -126 (limit -128): at most 2 more bytes. +26 bytes in the main block; the IF SKY_MODE wrapper keeps the 9-byte-free SKY_MODE=0 builds as they were. skeptics.reason: The opcodes are all real on the 65SC12 (BRA, INC A, STZ; no Rockwell bit ops). Bytes recounted at +26 (search_done &280E -> &2828 in the shipping listing). The SKIP 1 does put the DEX at &2800. Branch ranges hold: BPL check_if_friendly becomes -126, and every branch downstream stays in range. The rebased abs,X reads (base+1,X with X one lower) hit the same addresses in the &1344/&1366 tables, so no page crossings appear or disappear there. The inlined set_cm_left is instruction-for-instruction the same, and the two new self-modified operands are written only here. The refutation is about the cycle accounting. relies_on says the BPL back to the loop's top is 'the only hot crossing left'. In fact all 26 bytes of code after &280E move, and nothing absorbs the shift: the SKIP 9 at &28FE and the SKIP 8 at &2E16 move with it. Taken branches change crossing in about two dozen places. The worst is in sky_main's sky_draw. Its whole-row loop now crosses a page: BPL whole goes from &30ED -> &30D9 (same page) to &3107 -> &30F3. That adds +1 cycle on every taken iteration, about 25 a pass on seed 1 and about 17 with RIGHT held (build/grind/pc-seed1.json and pc-right.json: about 84 and 55 cycles a pass at &30ED). The loop runs once per four bytes of a helicopter's sky image per whole character row, so in helicopter-heavy scenes (--flight, which was not measured) it can cost more than the 60 cycles a pass the prefilter saves. Logic branches also change crossing in kill_hostile_mover_and_mover, um0db5_is_on_screen, not_vsync_2ee3 and update_enemy_helicopter, each worth only a few cycles a pass either way. The measured seed-1 and RIGHT totals may already include the sky cost, but the stated mechanism is wrong and the net cost in heavy-helicopter passes is unknown. A fix would keep sky_draw's loop on one page, for example by trimming padding after the window or aligning the loop, and then measure flights as well. Local recount per search: the setup saves about 15 cycles (JSR/RTS dropped, and the BRA crosses a page: 4). A mover rejected by the right test saves 2 and one rejected by the left test saves 6. A mover checked in full costs a net +2 (INX +2, re-entry CPX/BCC/DEX/BEQ +4, immediates -4).

\ close_over_overlaps: a shown mover that overlaps one coming off or going on, drawn before it
\ (decision 37: below it, in the order movers are drawn), comes off and goes back on too, so
\ overlapping movers are always drawn in slot order and taken off in reverse (a mover's save block
\ holds what was under it, earlier movers included; one drawn after it, over it, holds its bytes in
\ its own save, so it can come off and go back on alone). Over a
\ short list of the slots that matter: each one shown or going on, with a rectangle covering
\ where it is shown and where it goes, a column and two rows to spare.
.close_over_overlaps
{
    STZ list_n
    LDY #0
.gather
    CPY act_n
    BEQ gathered
    STY ren_k
    LDX act,Y
    STX ren_i
    TXA                             \ C = 0: CPY act_n found Y < act_n
    ADC boff
    TAY
    LDA rec_xh,Y
    CMP #&FF
    BNE shown
    LDA need,X
    AND #&40
    BNE going_on
    LDY ren_k                       \ not listed: the loop's tail, kept in gather's page
    INY
    BRA gather                      \ 65C02 opcode
.going_on
    JSR list_live                   \ going on, not shown: where it goes
    BRA listed                      \ 65C02 opcode
.shown
    JSR list_recorded               \ where it is shown...
    LDX ren_i
    BIT need,X                      \ 65C02 opcode: V = need bit 6
    BVC listed
new:
.next
    LDY ren_k
    INY
    CPY act_n                       \ each's test again, here (Y <= act_n: C is clear in the body when Y < act_n)
    BNE each + 4                    \ the body, past each's CPY act_n and BEQ done (zero page: 2 + 2 bytes)
.done
    RTS
    ASSERT act_n < &100             \ so CPY act_n is 2 bytes and each + 4 is the body
}

Everything from &1B3B to the SKIP unused_3400_original at &333F slides down 1 byte (absorbed there, 193 bytes free). I scripted the listing over that run: no branch starts or stops crossing a page; no label in it sits at a page start (so no table base moves from xx00 to xxFF); ASSERTed layouts (move_mover_* +6/same page, keys, um_next, add/subtract_Y_rows at &196A/&1971) still hold. Logic: s_ptr+1 comes from b_ptr+1 (raise_address's X, the flipped path wraps &80->&40), so &40-&7F; after SBC #2 (with possible borrow) &3D-&7D, ORA #&40 equals the old CMP/BCS/ADC #&40 there and C=1 (no borrow), as save_same_page already relies on; SBC #&F8 with C=1 equals CLC/ADC #8 in A and carry (and V). C=0 at save_on_page on both paths. No outside references to up_cell/up_in_ring/raised/save_on_page, no self-modified operands or code-as-data in the window. Caveat (batch): the alignment depends on nothing before &9BE8 moving.

Project lens: src/render.6502 is hand-written (not GENERATED), the lines are not protected (no raster-timed code, not the &0004-&001E bytes), no data, table, zero page or workspace moves and no new RAM: it reads and writes exactly s_ptr/v_ptr (&C2-&C5) and (v_ptr),Y as before, under the same paging (bank 4, ACCCON unchanged). Size is identical: old and new are both 52 bytes (TXA at &9BE8 to save_on_page at &9C1C in build/strykers.lst; the candidate's '54' is a miscount but the claim of 0 bytes holds), so nothing after it moves and the region's free space is untouched. BRA is a 65SC12 opcode. Labels up_cell/up_in_ring/raised/save_on_page are referenced only in the window. Semantics checked: s_ptr is always a screen address (&40-&7F high byte, from b_ptr), so SBC #2 cannot borrow (C=1) and ORA #&40 equals the old CMP/BCS/ADC #&40 (for any value below &40 it adds &40; values &40-&7F unchanged), the same ORA save_same_page already uses; SBC #&F8 with C=1 gives the same A, N, Z and carry as CLC/ADC #8 (V differs but ADC #11 rewrites V before anything reads it); LDY #10 leaves Y=10 and N/Z as INY did, and A is reloaded next; the page-crossing path's BRA lands on save_on_page with C=0 as the fall-through did. Same state, screen and sound on every path, including ones the proofs do not run (the routine is the renderer's column draw for every sprite, front end not involved). Timing: in the shipping build the new BCC save_on_page at &9BFE goes to &9C00/&9C1C in one page, the BMI not taken saves 2 cycles over the taken page-crossing BPL. Only caveat (speed, not correctness): gameplay and fullredraw builds lay this out at other addresses (&9956, &9C02), so the alignment gain there is not the same; the gate measures the shipping build.

All labels (.up_cell, .up_in_ring, .raised, .save_on_page) are local to draw_column's { } scope and referenced only inside the window; no label+N or table refers into it. Hot path (X >= 0): BMI not taken falls into .raised with A = X, N = 0, exactly as BPL raised arrived. LDY #10 = INY's Y (9 -> 10) and the same N/Z, both overwritten by the LDA after. Page-crossing v_ptr path: INC, CLC, BRA save_on_page reaches it with C = 0 and the same registers as the old fall-through. Rare path (X < 0): s_ptr lo -= &80, hi -= 2 + borrow; b_ptr/s_ptr high is in the 16K ring &40-&7F (the same ORA #&40 wrap is already used at save_same_page), so hi after SBC is &3D-&7F, ORA #&40 equals the old CMP/BCS/ADC #&40 (bits 6,7 clear for &3D-&3F, bit 6 set for &40-&7F) and C = 1 (no borrow). TXA; SBC #&F8 with C = 1 gives X + 8 with carry out iff X >= &F8, identical A, N, Z, C to CLC; ADC #8 (V: adding +8 to a negative cannot overflow in either; V is dead anyway, ADC #11 rewrites it). Loop exit: BRA raised with A = X, C = 1, as the old fall-through; .raised's ORA/STA/LDY keep C and CLC precedes the ADC #11. D is clear in the renderer (and the old ADC depended on it equally). Memory writes are the same bytes in the same order (s_ptr lo then hi, the record's bytes), so irq1_handler sees nothing different; no stack use. Bytes: 52 before and after in the changed lines (0 saved). Cycles: hot path BPL taken across a page (4) -> BMI not taken (2), LDY #10 = INY (2): 2 saved per hot execution given the stated alignment; the page-crossing v_ptr path pays +3 for the BRA and the rare path about +6 per entry, as the claim says.

All ds_*/dm_*/b_ptr operands are zero page (listing: ds_clip &51, dm_jmin &5A, dm_jmax &5C, ds_n &68, dm_slot &58). Bytes: the old code is 57 bytes from LDA straight_sprite_hi to LDA dm_slot, the new 61 (+4; the claim says -4 saved, which matches). Branch ranges: BRA generic is &3B forward, and BCC/BNE rds_clip_g32 is about -&33. The C sense is right: CMP ds_n with A=jmax gives C=1 when n<=jmax, the old BCC/BEQ no_clip. Only the recovery delay after the rising edge goes: the chip's constraint is write enable low for >=8us (wait_low, 17 cycles from STZ's write to the high write, untouched); after the rise, the data bus is next changed by a STA sysvia_ora_nh no earlier than 31 cycles later on any path (RTS 6 + the caller's amplitude/period arithmetic or sfx_silence's loop, counted per path: tone low->high 44, high->amplitude 31, noise->amplitude 33, silence 44), and by the main program or the MOS only after RTS/RTS/PLA/STA/PLA/PLY/PLX/RTI.

Cycles: old tail after wait_low LDY#8 2 + STY 4 + LDY#4 2 + DEY/BNE x4 (4*2+3*3+2=19) + RTS 6 = 33; new LDA#8 2 + STA 4 + RTS 6 = 12; saves 21 (the following 1 MHz VIA access may shift its stretch by +/-1 since 21 is odd, a nominal-count caveat only). Removes a hardware-timing delay that the driver's documented design keeps on purpose: src/lib/sfx50.6502's header (lines 15-16) says the chip is written 'as the MOS writes it ... with the MOS's delays', and sfx_write's comment says 'as MOS 3.20 writes it (&F5E6)'; the MOS has the same LDY #4 / DEY / BNE settle after write enable goes high. Dropping it changes how the SN76489 is driven on real hardware (the 1 MHz slow-bus port A data and latch line 0), which no emulator proof here can see. The candidate admits this ('a hardware-timing change the emulator cannot show'), and its claim that the chip needs no recovery time after the rising edge is recalled, not measured. That breaks the project's 'Measure, do not recall' rule and rule 1 (same sound as the original on the real machine), and it is a deviation from the driver's agreed design (decision 25) with no decision behind it. Same-length padding (SKIP 5) and the register reasoning (A dead, Y=0 on exit, X kept) do check out, but the timing premise cannot be verified, so it is refuted. Recount: 21 cycles per call saved (LDY #4 2, then 3 x (DEY 2 + BNE taken 3) and DEY 2 + BNE not taken 2 = 19); 0 bytes (5 freed, padded).

Stack unchanged (one RTS either way). Interrupts are off throughout (sfx_tick in the IRQ, sfx_silence SEI); after the rising edge the next port A/latch write is at least ~27 cycles away on every in-module path (shortest: ended in the request loop with X=0 then the noise channel's write, ~64 cycles to the next write-enable low), and the interrupted main program (keydown_int) or the MOS can only touch the VIA after RTS..RTI, more than 30 cycles. The write-enable low hold (wait_low) is unchanged; MOS's post-high delay is only needed against an immediately following chip write, which never happens here. Cycles: removed LDY #4 (2) + 3x(DEY 2 + BNE 3) + DEY 2 + BNE 2 = 21; LDA#/STA replace LDY#/STY at equal cost. Bytes: 0.

A differs (written byte -> &08) and Z differs (1 -> 0): every consumer overwrites both before reading - sfx_output reloads A (LDA sfx_p_hi / LDA sfx_v), sfx_tick goes to LDA sfx_dp,X or DEX/BPL then LDA, its RTS returns to irq1_handler which PLAs, sfx_silence DEX/BPL then PLP (flags restored) and its two bank 5 callers reload A (LDA #&FF / CLI then JMP clear_title_screen after LDA? - give_irq_back: CLI, JMP; take_irq_for_play: LDA #&FF). VIA state at exit identical (DDRA &FF, ORA the byte, latch line 0 high written with the same value &08). Interrupts: sfx_write runs only in irq1_handler or under sfx_silence's SEI, so nothing interleaves; a main-program keydown_int interrupted mid-sequence sees the same ORA/DDRA as before. Timing at the chip: WE-low time (wait_low) unchanged; rise to the next ORA write is >= 31 cycles (tone high->amplitude: RTS 6, LDA abs,X 4, 4 LSR 8, EOR 2, ORA abs,X 4, BRA 3, STA 4), next WE fall later still, longer than the MOS's own post-rise delay; after sfx_silence returns, the MOS's next chip write comes after DEX/BPL/PLP/RTS/CLI and an IRQ entry. The 5-byte slide of .noise, sfx_silence, the sfx tables, sfx_data, compiled_bank5 and credits is label-relative everywhere (sfx_next_ramp's inline reads compute page+offset+Y with absolute,Y carry; noise_written's sentinel is a high byte >= &A5, still never 0-7); its page-crossing cycles and the 'no data moves' rule are for the machine and project lenses.

    LDY #4
new:
STY sysvia_orb                  \ and high again
    LDY #2
summary: Conservative alternative (overlaps the first two): keep the structure and shorten the post-high delay loop from 4 to 2 passes (19 -> 9 cycles), same bytes, nothing moves.
equivalence: Only the number of iterations of a pure DEY/BNE delay changes; the loop still exits with Y=0, Z=1, N=0 and leaves A, X, C, V alone, so register and flag state at the RTS is identical. The recovery after the write-enable rise falls from 27 to 17 cycles (LDY, loop, RTS: 2+9+6) before any following chip write, and every path then spends >=31 more cycles before the next STA sysvia_ora_nh, so the gap from the rise to the next chip write is >=48 cycles (24us) against the chip's 8us (32 clocks at 4 MHz).
relies_on: No byte moves (LDY #4 and LDY #2 are both two bytes), so no page crossing changes; the loop stays inside &A59E-&A5A3 on page &A5. wait_low (the 8us write-enable hold) is untouched. Hardware timing the emulator cannot show; this is the minimal-risk way to take cycles from the delay.

skeptics.reason: Machine lens: only the immediate of LDY changes (A0 04 -> A0 02, both 2 bytes, 2 cycles), so nothing moves; listing has wait_high at &A5A0, BNE at &A5A1 branching back to &A5A0, same page, no +1. Old loop 4 DEY (8) + 3 taken BNE (9) + 1 untaken (2) = 19; new 2 DEY (4) + 1 taken (3) + 1 untaken (2) = 9: 10 cycles saved per sfx_write, exit state identical (Y=0, Z=1, N=0; A, X, C, V untouched; sfx_silence's 'Y = 0' note still holds). No self-modified operand or data read in sfx_write (no stores to wait_high/sfx_write+n in src). wait_low (WE-low hold) unchanged. Shortest gap from WE rise to the next STA sysvia_ora_nh with the new loop: tone low->high byte path LDY#2+loop+RTS (17) + LDA abs,X 4 + 4 LSR 8 + EOR 2 + ORA abs,X 4 + BRA 3 = 38 cycles (19us); sfx_silence's next channel ~50; both well over the chip's 8us (32 clocks at 4 MHz), and the SN76489 completes a write while WE is low, so the post-rise wait is margin only. No raster-timed code depends on sfx_write's length.

The count is right (LDY #4 loop 2+8+11=21 cycles, LDY #2 loop 2+4+5=11: 10 a call, 0 bytes, no page crossing), but this is hardware-timed code the project deliberately keeps as the MOS writes it: sfx50.6502's header says the chip is written 'as the MOS writes it ... with the MOS's delays' and sfx_write cites MOS 3.20 &F5E6, whose LDY #4 post-high wait this copies (decision 25's driver, reusable). Shortening it changes the SN76489 write-enable/port-A timing, which jsbeeb cannot model, so no proof in the gate can show the sound is unchanged on a real machine (rule 1: same sound; 'measure, do not recall'): the candidate's own relies_on concedes 'hardware timing the emulator cannot show'. Its >=31-cycle argument covers only the driver's own next chip write; it does not cover the VIA traffic that follows sfx_silence in give_irq_back (PLP, RTS, CLI, then the MOS's interrupt, its 100 Hz tick and keyboard scan drive port A with DDRA changed and its own OSWORD 7 sound writes) or what follows the vsync handler's RTI (keydown_int writes port A/ORB from the main loop), where the gap from WE high to the next port A write shrinks from 27+ to 17+ cycles. Whether the chip needs that tail is not established here; a deviation from the MOS's write timing would need an agreed decision and a real-hardware check (beeb-cross-emulator), not a grind batch. Unsure, so refuted.

Only the LDY immediate at &A59E changes (A0 04 -> A0 02), so no byte moves and wait_high (&A5A0-&A5A2) stays on page &A5. Nothing else references wait_high or the operand: a grep of src and tools finds no label+N, self-modification or table entry. All entries reach these lines by falling through from wait_low: sfx_write, ddra_set_c046b (JSR from sfx_output line 157, BRA line 165, BRA from sfx_next_ramp.ended, JSR from noise line 203 and from sfx_silence via ended). The loop still exits with Y=0, Z=1, N=0, and A, X, C, V and D are untouched (callers rely on Y=0: sfx_silence's comment). The stack is unchanged and there is one exit, the RTS. Interrupts: every caller runs with I set (sfx_tick inside the vsync IRQ; sfx_silence does PHP/SEI), so no interrupt can land between the writes. Hardware: wait_low, the write-enable low hold, is unchanged, and the datasheet needs nothing after WE rises. The shortest path from the rise to the next data change is the tone's amplitude write: LDY#2 2 + loop 9 + RTS 6 + LDA,X 4 + 4xLSR 8 + EOR 2 + ORA,X 4 + BRA 3 = 38 cycles (19us). The argument says >=48 and that is overstated, but the gap is still well over 8us before the next STZ write-enable. The source comment 'with the MOS's delays' becomes slightly stale. Cycles: old LDY#4 + 4 passes = 2+19 = 21, new 2+9 = 11, saves 10. Bytes: 0.

The rare range entry (helicopter boarding) moves out of line in front of the player's entry, stores its own operands (low from mover_x_max_low, &17 + 3) and BRAs into the shared STA cm_full_below_operand: +3 cycles on a path that runs once per boarding attempt. Also get_mover_X_type_and_height's skeleton test as LDA frame / EOR #&0D / ASL A / BEQ (Z iff frame AND &7F = &0D), one byte shorter, same 4 cycles. Alternatives: candidate 2 (same without the EOR byte, +4) and candidate 3 (the EOR byte alone); this overlaps both.

Order of the three operand stores is immaterial (set_cm_left, the next call, reads none of them). Flags at exit: A, N, Z from the same LDA mover_x_max_high; C differs (old 1, new whatever the callee left) and is dead: set_cm_left begins LDA zp / SEC. Rare path: old entered at the label with last_mover = &17: LDA last_mover/CLC/ADC #3 = &1A -> cm_full_below_operand, then x_max_low -> its operand, then LDA high. summary: subtract_delta_from_screen_address_in_AX: the ring wrap CMP #&40 / BCS / ADC #&40 becomes ORA #&40 (A = 1..&7F for a screen address), 3 cycles saved on the common taken-BCS path (4 when the wrap is needed); the 4 freed bytes are a SKIP after the RTS so nothing after moves.
equivalence: Inputs: X (address high) is a screen high byte, &40-&7F on every path (movers_screen_address_high starts 0 and is only written from this routine's and the add's outputs and the player's; screen_start/edge/mover addresses are ring-wrapped &40-&7F), delta_high_table <= &3E. So hi' = X - dh - borrow lies in [1,&7F] (X=&40,dh=&3E,borrow: 1; X=0 inactive mover: 0 - dh - b gives 0 or &FF/&FE, all handled below). For hi' < &40 (bit 6 clear, bit 7 clear): original adds &40, ORA #&40 sets bit 6 = adds &40: equal. For hi' in &40-&7F: original unchanged, ORA leaves bit 6 set: equal. For the inactive-mover case hi'=&FE/&FF/0: &FE,&FF unchanged in both (bit 6 set), 0 -> &40 both. The only inputs where they differ are hi' in &80-&BF, which needs X >= &80 + dh: never a screen address. A, X, Y at the RTS are the same (TAX/TYA unchanged; Y = low sum). Flags: the original left C from CMP/ADC, N/Z from TYA (unchanged), V from SBC; now C and V are the SBC's. Every caller of subtract_delta (1050, 1842, 2859, 4218, shield.rewind) and, through subtract_Y_rows/rows_up, (1948, 1965, 2883, 4221) goes on with STX/STA/LDY/LDA/DEC/JMP that set or ignore flags; none branches on C or V before writing them. The branch from add's wrap (BRA skip_wraparound_1d66) still lands on TAX. Not a bug-for-bug difference on any path the original reaches.
relies_on: No page crossing moves: the whole routine, both delta tables and the rows routines stay in page &19 (&1931-&1969 in the bench build); the SKIP 4 keeps subtract_Y_rows_from_screen_address_in_AX at &196A and everything after in place, so BEQ leave_1d68 (now -7 and -14 bytes, same page) and every later hot branch are unchanged. leave_1d68 moves 4 bytes earlier (&1969 -> &1967); its three users are all short relative branches in page &19. The BRA from add's wrap becomes 2 bytes shorter, still in page. Gameplay builds (GAMEPLAY_ANY) compile the SKIP out, as the file's other padding does. Relies on the screen-address invariant X in &40-&7F (and 0 for never-plotted movers) for the subtract callers.

skeptics.reason: The opcodes, cycles (old 5 taken / 6 wrap, new 2: 3-4 saved) and bytes (6 -> 2, 4 saved, SKIP 4 keeps the rest in place) are right, and no caller reads C or V afterwards (checked 1050, 1842 loop's CPY, 2859 -> move_mover's SEC, 4218 -> CPX, shield rewind -> start_column PHP/PLP then SEC). But the equivalence rests on X in &40-&7F or 0, and that is false: the inputs where ORA #&40 differs (result &80-&BF) are reachable. movers_screen_address_high starts 0 (EQUB table) and update_mover moves any mover not beyond viewport_right+10, with no left bound and no requirement that it was ever placed by calculate_screen_addresses_for_mover_on_edge. From 0: subtract with a borrow gives &FF (the candidate admits this); add_delta_to_screen_address_in_AX on &FF with no carry from the low byte gives &FF, N set, and its own wrap (SBC #&3F) stores &BF. A further subtract then gives &BF/&BE in the original (CMP #&40: BCS, unchanged) but &FF/&FE with ORA #&40. Concrete: a never-placed mover at 0:&00 moves left twice (&FF:&F0), right once (&F8, no carry -> &BF:&F8), left once (&BF:&F0): original X=&BF, candidate X=&FF. An enemy helicopter patrolling min..max (turns at both ends) in a never-used slot does exactly this over one patrol (40 columns left, then right: &FE+0 -> wrap &BE, ...). movers_screen_address_high is game state (passlock compares it) and the renderer places a mover by it (render.6502 list_live / world_of_address), so the state, and possibly the drawn position of a mover that reaches the view without an edge pass, differ from the original.

The invariant the equivalence rests on (X entering subtract_delta is &40-&7F, or 0 for a never-plotted mover) is false, and the two codes differ for a result in &80-&BF. movers_screen_address_high starts &00 (src/game.6502:842). No add_new_movers path writes it, so a mover in a fresh slot keeps 0 until the edge calculation runs. If that mover moves left (move_mover_left -> subtract_delta, Y=0, low byte < 8 borrows), it gets &00-&00-1 = &FF, kept by both codes. If it then moves right, add_delta_to_screen_address_in_AX gives &FF+0 with N set, so wrap_add_delta_g4566 subtracts &40 and leaves &BF (or &FE -> &BE). If it moves left again, subtract gives &BF/&BE: the original's CMP #&40/BCS keeps &BF/&BE, but ORA #&40 gives &FF/&FE. That is a different movers_screen_address_high (stored at 2979 via mover_screen_address_high). The renderer reads it (record_live/world_of_address, draw's dm_scr_hi, the record compare at render.6502:2368) and so do projectiles fired from that mover (4203-4227). This is state the passlock oracle compares, so the change is not equivalent on every path. The flags are fine: C differs only in the wrap and inactive cases, and every continuation writes C before reading it (CPY/CPX/SEC/ASL; start_column's PLP carries it on to scroll_screen_left, then ASL or SEC). V is the same. The SKIP 4 keeps subtract_Y_rows and the self-modified JSR's page in place. But the value range is wrong, so it is refuted.

\ world_of_address: AX = a screen address; wa_x (16 bits) and wa_y = the world column and the y
\ (movers_y's sense: &C7 at the top row) of that byte, by the view in zero page (its screen
\ start and viewport_left). A character row is &280 bytes: the row is guessed from the offset's
\ high byte (wa_rows_guess, out by at most one) and settled against wa_rows_base.
\ BUGS #10: a mover clipped at the view's left edge (x 1-11 left of viewport_left) has its
\ address left of its row's first column, which is the end of the row above (column 69-79) - or,
\ in the first row, the ring's hidden 48 columns past the last (row 25): placed there it would be
\ 80 columns right and 8 lines up. Column 69-79 is the row above only if the mover is not left of
\ the view (dm_slot = its slot: its x, 80 columns left of that place if it is); row 25 is always
\ the first row's left. Its place is then the address's column in the row below, left of the

\ nothing wraps: a mover goes on only with x <= viewport_right, so its address is in its row

equivalence: Old loop, Y = n >= 1 times: A += 8 (low byte), on a carry X += 1 and X = &40 if that makes it &80 or more. New: A = A + 8*n in one ADC: C = 0 after ASL A x3 because 8*n <= 96 (n <= 12, see relies_on), so the ADC can carry out at most once, which is the sum of the old loop's carries (a second carry would need 8n >= 256); the wrap test (INX, BPL, LDX #&40) is then taken once, exactly as the single old carry. Without a carry X is untouched, as before. Exit: Y = 0 (LDY #0), columns_to_clip_from_left = 0, as the old DEY loop left them; what follows (STY delta_high, LDY #8, STY delta_low) is unchanged and overwrites delta_low, which this code uses as scratch for the old A (nothing reads delta_low in between: game zero page, not touched by the interrupt). Flags at exit are dead (LDY #8 follows). A, X on exit are the screen address as before.

equivalence: The old code took the three movers of the chain (base b, next n, next after c; the base advanced to the one after c), copied their raster ys, then three times picked the slot with the lowest copied raster y (a later slot winning a tie: slot 2 = b, 1 = n, 0 = c), marked it FF, and called update_mover on it. The pick order is therefore the stable ascending sort of [b, n, c] by raster y (ties keep the chain order); the copies are a snapshot taken before any update_mover, and so are the compares of the new code, all done before the first call. Raster ys are result_high of times_78 (at most &4D, written only at movers_raster_y,Y in the mover update), so never equal to the FF marker and no marked slot could be re-picked in the old code. The new code stores b, n, c to slot 0, 1, 2, advances the base exactly as before (um_next chain, stored before any call), then runs a bubble sort with strict-less swaps: cs(1,2) (swap if r(slot 2) < r(slot 1)), cs(0,1) (swap if r(slot 1) < r(slot 0), and then back to cs(1,2)), exit when cs(0,1) does not swap straight after cs(1,2). Register state at each label: umsort_loop X = id of slot 1, Y = id of slot 2 (from populate; from the swap-back, reloaded from the slots); umsort_slot_0 X = id of slot 1 (swap path: reloaded after the exchange); at umsort_done Y = id of slot 0 (set by LDY just before the BCS). summary: The whole-row copy (94 bytes a pass, 13.75 cycles a byte) made self-modifying: four LDA abs,Y / STA abs,Y sites whose operands are set once a whole row from d_ptr and s_ptr (76 cycles, 16 stores), so each byte costs 4+5+2 instead of 5+6+2: 2 cycles a byte against 76 a row. The part path (line8) and its pointers are untouched; d_ptr/s_ptr are still stored. Alternative to the second candidate (the unroll by 8), which it beats; they overlap.
equivalence: Same bytes copied in the same order (Y from the row's top byte down to 0, one DEY after each), same loop (BPL sdw_l1 on N after the fourth DEY, so the row's 8k bytes need the same multiple of 4 as before), same exits: BMI next_row always taken (Y=&FF..), A the last byte loaded, X untouched (next_row reloads it from sky_q), d_ptr/s_ptr unchanged in zero page. LDA abs,Y and STA abs,Y compute the same 16-bit address as the (zp),Y forms (low + Y, carry into the high byte, wrap at &FFFF); the page-cross +1 on the load is the same condition. The operands are set before the loop on every whole row, from the pointers as sky_row left them (A and Y are not used between: Z set, Y the top byte is kept). Part rows (BNE part) jump over the whole block; they never run the patched sites. The patches write the RAM the code runs from (ACCCON X: shadow's copy of &30xx when drawing the shadow screen, as the existing STA cell+1 does), and render_reset copies the whole of &3000-&3FFF main to shadow, so both copies carry the sites. No interrupt runs or reads these bytes. Built and run: tools/passlock.mjs plain build against the current one, 2,500 passes seed 1 with --screen: state identical, 0 screen bytes differing.
relies_on: Whole rows: Y+1 is a multiple of 8 (sky_geom's ry = 8*(d2-d1)+7 or, past &7FFF, 0 - rl - 8 with rl a multiple of 8), as before; the window's own BNE part / BMI next_row ranges (part now 88 bytes away: assembles, +162 would not; BMI next_row still 66). Measured on the plain build, pcprof 1500 passes seed 1: render 23432 -> 23284 cycles a pass (-148), and with SKIP 16 or 48 added before line8 (image at &31CF, &31EF) 23287 and 23293, so not an alignment accident. Uses 64 of the 193 free bytes at the end of the main block (unused_3400_original SKIP; gameplay builds have 13 more).

skeptics.reason: Machine lens: all opcodes are NMOS-era (LDA/STA abs,Y, LDA/STA abs, LDA zp), real on the 65SC12. abs,Y forms the same 16-bit effective address as (zp),Y (wrap at &FFFF), so rows past &7FFF behave identically; the load's page-cross +1 is the same condition; STA abs,Y is a flat 5 vs STA (zp),Y 6. Per byte 4+5+2=11 vs 5+6+2=13 (crossings equal), BPL/BMI unchanged; setup 4 x LDA zp (3) + 16 x STA abs (4) = 76. Bytes: setup 56 + loop 28 vs 20 = +64 (claim -64 = grows 64). Listing: old loop &30D9-&30EF in page &30; new sdw_l1 &3111, BPL at &312D, next &312F: no branch page cross. BNE part now 88 bytes forward, BPL 30 back, BMI next_row 66 (unchanged): all in range. line8 moves &3104->&3144, entries to &3167, HI(line8) still computed (cell+2 written), so the existing self-mod is intact. The new self-modified operands are written in the same instruction stream, same ACCCON X as execution, like cell+1; render_reset copies &3000-&3FFF main to shadow so both copies carry the code; nothing else references sky_draw.whole. sky_zero (&317E..) loops stay in page &31; per-screen vars and sky_img0 (&31BF..&337F) move, sky_blk_lo/hi built from the label, SKY_IMG_SIZE ends at &337F under &3400 (free SKIP shrinks 193->129; ASSERT at game.6502:5333 guards gameplay builds). Only the cycle claim is overstated: window counts give BMI next_row 4.4 cycles/pass = 1.47 whole rows/pass (not 1.1) and ~94.6 bytes/pass, so savings ~2*94.6-76*1.47 = ~78 cycles/pass, ~53 per execution (2*64 bytes - 76), image page-cross shifts aside; still a net gain, consistent with the measured -148 render cycles.

Project lens: sky_draw is hand-written (not GENERATED, not PROTECTED, not raster-timed; no 'sky_draw.*+' entry or external reference to .whole - only JSR sky_draw from src/sky.6502:248). It runs from main RAM &30xx/&31xx called from bank 4; with ACCCON X set both the code fetch and the patch stores hit shadow's copy, exactly as the existing self-modified 'cell' JMP does, and every operand is set immediately before its use on every whole row, so render_reset's main->shadow copy carrying stale operands is harmless. LDA abs,Y/STA abs,Y read the image (&31xx-&33xx / SKY_IMG1 &3E40) and write the screen in the same RAM the (zp),Y forms did under the same ACCCON; ANDY/ROMSEL irrelevant (&3000-&7FFF). No zero page or new RAM used; d_ptr/s_ptr still written and unchanged. Room: +64 bytes (old whole block 24 bytes, new 88) into the 193-byte SKIP before unused_3400_original (&333F), ASSERTed; sky_main is only assembled with SKY_MODE, gameplay builds have 13 more. The only data that moves is sky_main's own per-screen state and sky_img0 (+64, &317F->&31BF, ending &337F < &3400), reached only by label (sky_blk tables in sky.6502, symbol-loading harnesses); the builder in HAZEL is address-independent; nothing from &3400 moves. Branches: BNE part +86, BMI next_row, BPL back all in range. Behaviour identical on all paths: the sky helicopter drawing is the only user, same bytes, same order, same exits (A last byte, flags N set). Note for docs: CLAUDE.md's sky_img0 &317F and 193 free bytes would need updating. Cycles: per whole row 2 per byte saved (11.75 vs 13.75) minus 76 setup; ~94 at the claimed average.

Semantics hold on every path. Entries: only fall-through from JSR sky_row/BNE part (label whole is scope-local, no other references to sky_draw internals; sky_draw's only caller is sky.6502:248). Part rows branch over the new block (BNE part now +88, in range) and never run the patched sites; the set-up runs on every whole row before the loop, from d_ptr/s_ptr as computed (A, Y untouched between: Y kept as the top byte, the loads/stores of the set-up do not touch Y or X). LDA abs,Y / STA abs,Y compute the same address as (zp),Y including the carry into the high byte and the &FFFF wrap, so the same bytes are read and written in the same order. Loop condition identical (BPL after the 4th DEY), exit identical (BMI next_row always, Y=&FC..&FF as before), A at exit the last byte loaded as before, X reloaded from sky_q, flags at RTS from CPX as before; d_ptr/s_ptr (&C0-&C3) still hold the same values afterwards; no stack change. Self-modified operands are written and fetched in the same RAM: ACCCON X steers all CPU accesses to &3000-&7FFF (fetches included), set once by cpu_sees_back before drawing, as the existing STA cell+1 already relies on. The interrupt (irq1_handler) read-modify-writes ACCCON preserving X with the render's SEI discipline, touches no &31xx code bytes, and its variables are below &3000, so it neither sees nor disturbs the patched operands. Cost is non-semantic: the 76-cycle set-up loses on rows under 38 bytes (2 a byte saved), so the per-execution gain depends on row widths; the measured -148 render cycles a pass is for the other lenses to accept.

summary: ALT 1 (best; overlaps ALT 2 and 3, the same code with a different pad): the column's col_ptr advance without reloading rows_m1 (new low byte kept in Y while the first row is read at the old pointer), the rare page crossing in its own block after JMP next, and a 12-byte SKIP in that dead zone that moves the bank-4 code after it onto better page alignment.
equivalence: Same arithmetic: A = count-1 (the DEC A), then SEC; ADC #2; ADC col_ptr, as the old LDA rows_m1/SEC/ADC #2/ADC col_ptr did (rows_m1 is still stored for the cell loop). The new low byte waits in Y (TAY leaves C) while SBC (col_ptr) reads the first row at the OLD pointer, then STY col_ptr. A carry (page crossing, rare) goes to each_cross: same SBC with the high byte not yet advanced, STY col_ptr, INC col_ptr+1, rejoin at on_same_page. At on_same_page col_ptr (both bytes), X (the line) and rows_m1 equal the old values on both paths. Differences left: A (old new low byte, new the line), Y (old 8, new the new low byte), C: every successor overwrites them before reading (clip_test loads ds_n/ds_c, visible loads b_ptr, raised LDY #9, save_on_page TAY; C is not live: annotations show C=?). col_ptr is written later than before but nothing reads it between (renderer scratch, not the interrupt's). Entries (JMP each, BRA each, BPL/BCC draw_column.each, BEQ empty) unchanged; each_cross sits after JMP next, reached only by BCS each_cross (about 22 bytes back; its BRA about 30 forward). Overflow case (count >= 254) has the same arithmetic as before. SKIP in the dead zone is never executed.

Without the pad (ALT 3) it is -19/-26: the code itself is 2 cycles x 10.8 non-empty columns; the rest is alignment (render -40, and logic -33 from a branch after it no longer crossing). BPL raised crosses &9B->&9C in the control (+1 taken, about 9 columns a pass); with this pad the BPL's next instruction is at &9C00, so it no longer crosses. BCC/BEQ visible, BMI clip_test, BEQ empty stay on &9B; the .byte, .part_byte and .cell loops stay within one page. skeptics.reason: The code change itself is correct for the 65SC12: all opcodes real (DEC A, SBC (zp), BRA are 65C02; no Rockwell ops). Recount: the common path goes from 28 to 26 cycles after STA (v_ptr),Y, so it saves 2. The rare page-crossing path goes from 32 to 35. Branch ranges assemble: BCS each_cross is -33, BRA on_same_page +29, BEQ empty -73, BMI clip_test -77, BPL/BCC draw_column.each 91/78. The arithmetic is the same, including count>=254. But the 21 bytes it adds to bank 4 (12 of them the SKIP pad) break other builds. I assembled HEAD 9f97ad5 with and without the edit in a private copy. Shipping config: OK. SKY_HELI=0 (the decision-36 kind cache build, make DEFINES=SKY_HELI=0): fails with 'bank 4 overruns the renderer's workspace by 12' (the control has 9 bytes spare, PAD_END at &B3F7). DEBUG_FULLREDRAW=1, the proof gate's oracle: fails with 'overruns by 14' (the control has 7 spare). The oracle not assembling means the gate cannot run, and CLAUDE.md requires every flag set to build. The alignment claim is also incomplete. With the code after .each moved 21 bytes: BPL raised, BCC up_cell, BEQ in_hazel, BNE gather and BEQ gathered stop crossing a page. The logic itself looked equivalent (same A = count-1 into SEC/ADC #2/ADC col_ptr, SBC (col_ptr) at the old pointer, Y/A/C dead after on_same_page, col_ptr renderer scratch &C7/&C8 not read by the interrupt, no entries past labels), but a change that breaks a flag combination's assembly fails SKILL.md 'Room'. Semantics hold on every path. Entries to the changed lines: .each (BRA each at draw_column, JMP each x4 from next_c/step_forward/to_each, BPL/BCC draw_column.each from ren_draw_sprite), unchanged; each_cross is reached only by its BCS (after JMP next, nothing falls into it; the SKIP 12 is unreachable). Arithmetic: A = count-1 after DEC/STA rows_m1/STA (v_ptr),Y (STA leaves flags), then SEC; ADC #2; ADC col_ptr equals the old LDA rows_m1; SEC; ADC #2; ADC col_ptr bit for bit, including C for count >= 254. SBC (col_ptr) reads at the unmodified pointer on both new paths, as the old did (old stored col_ptr after the SBC). At on_same_page: col_ptr lo/hi, X, rows_m1, (v_ptr)+8 identical; differences are A (old new low byte / new the line), Y (old 8 / new the new low byte), C, and Z after BIT ds_clip (A-dependent). None is live: BMI reads only N (from memory); clip_test overwrites A (LDA ds_c / LDA ds_n), reads no Y/C/Z before CMP; visible overwrites A at LDA b_ptr, Y first written by LDY #9 at raised, C set by SEC in up_cell / CLC before use; next sets SEC; next_c's paths reach JMP each (LDY #1) or done: RTS. At done Y differs (old 8 on the clipped-last-column path, but normal exits leave Y = stop_y anyway); callers never read Y after ren_draw_sprite/draw_mover returns (render.6502 1540-1556: LDX/LDA/TAY; 1383: LDY dm_index; sky.6502 261 then .kept: LDX/LDA/STA; part_three falls into the same). Flags at RTS come from DEC ds_c, same. Interrupt: col_ptr (&C7) is renderer scratch; irq1_handler does not touch it (the &C7 aliases multiplicand/target_address are logic-only, multiply_A_by_X_2f1e is not called from the IRQ), so the later store is invisible. Stack: no pushes, unchanged. Branch ranges all well inside 127 (BCS back ~33, BRA fwd 29, BEQ empty back ~73, BMI clip_test back ~77, BPL draw_column.each fwd ~91). Recount: the non-crossing path 28 -> 26 cycles (2 a non-empty column); the claimed 6.8 includes page-alignment effects of the SKIP that I did not re-measure (the machine/project lens); the crossing path 30 -> 33 (+3, rare). Bytes: +9 code, +12 SKIP = bank 4 grows 21.

LDA zone_hi,X                   \ d's high byte less 1 into span_d + 1 ...
    SBC span_x_hi
summary: span_in_zone's loop: drop the CLC before SBC span_x_hi; C is 0 at every entry to .each. 2 cycles an iteration, 1 byte smaller (slides everything after &9741 down one byte: see relies_on). Alternative to candidate 1's loop half, disjoint from candidate 2.
equivalence: Loop: .each is entered with C = 0 on every path. From the prefix: CLC; ADC #2 on A = a width from mover_types_width_table (max &0B = MOVER_WIDEST; span_in_zone's single caller is render.6502:456) gives C = 0, and STA, LDA, BNE, DEC zp, LDX, BEQ keep C. From .next (the only other way to .each, via TXA; BNE each): .next is reached by BNE next after ADC #0, taken only when the result is non-zero, and then the carry out is 0 (a carry out needs A + C = 256, which gives 0), or by falling out of BCS hit not taken, so C = 0; TXA keeps C. With C = 0, SBC span_x_hi is exactly CLC; SBC span_x_hi (zone_hi - span_x_hi - 1), and every later instruction is unchanged, so span_d, span_d + 1 and the final C are identical.
relies_on: Width table <= 253, single caller; .next only reached with C = 0. Moves every byte after &9741 down by one (rest of span_in_zone, .lives, width_of_type_A, mark_to_draw and on to the end of render.6502's code in bank 4), so a branch or indexed table read elsewhere may start or stop crossing a page; not counted here, which is why candidate 1 pairs the CLC drop with a +1 byte change instead.

skeptics.reason: Locally correct (C=0 on every entry to .each: CLC;ADC #2 on widths <= &0B, and .next only after BNE on a non-zero ADC #0 result or an untaken BCS; SBC zp is 3 cycles either way, so the loop saves the CLC's 2 cycles and 1 byte). But the byte removed at &9740 slides every byte after it in DATA1 down by one, with no ALIGN before REN_BASE: the rest of the renderer (&9741-&A365), sprite_column_count, ck_index, the ck_* and straight_sprite tables and all the straight sprites (&A530-&B3xx). Scanning every branch in &9741-&A365: record_differs' first BNE out (listing &9FFE, D0 2E, next &A000 -> &A02E, same page) becomes &9FFD with next &9FFF -> &A02D, a page crossing: +1 cycle every time a record's type differs from its live slot (render.6502:446, called per shown record per pass). Indexed tables also move: ck_index &A3B2 (crossing from X>=&4E, becomes X>=&4F) and straight_sprite_hi &A4E4 (X>=&1C becomes X>=&1D) each lose one crossing index, and every straight sprite's data starts one byte lower, changing which rows/columns take draw_column's page-crossing paths (.on_same_page/.data_same_page/.save_same_page) in an uncounted direction. The candidate itself says the shift is not counted; the net per-pass effect (claimed 1.5 cycles) is therefore not established, and it has at least one concrete new cost. Not proven, so refuted; candidate 1's pairing with a +1-byte change (keeping the layout) is the safe form.

Entries to .each: (1) fall-through from BEQ lives not taken; C comes from CLC; ADC #2 on A = mover_types_width_table[rec_type AND &7F] (single caller render.6502:456; table entries <= &0B, valid types < &1C; even the tables after it hold no byte >= &FE), so C=0, and STA/LDA/BNE/DEC zp/DEC zp/LDX/BEQ keep C. (2) from .next via TXA; BNE each: .next is reached by BNE next after ADC #0 (non-zero result means no carry out, C=0) or by BCS hit not taken (C=0); TXA keeps C. No other reference to .each or to span_in_zone+N (grep of src and tools); sky_edges only reads zone_n. With C=0, SBC span_x_hi == CLC; SBC span_x_hi on A, all flags (the following STA/LDA overwrite N/Z, SEC overwrites C, V dead), span_d+1 identical; no stack or interrupt-visible change (interrupts see no different memory; CLC changed no shared state). Saves CLC: 2 cycles an iteration, 1 byte. The one-byte shift of the code after it is a layout/page-crossing question for the gate, not semantics.

Low bytes differ (Z=0): BEQ not taken, falls into .more with A = v_ptr low, which .more does not use (first instruction LDY #10), registers/flags as the old BNE-taken path (flags from CMP, nothing reads them). Low bytes equal: BEQ to .cols_low_eq, which does the old second half unchanged: LDA v_ptr+1 / CMP rb_end+1, BNE more (A = v_ptr+1 on arrival at .more, as in the old code, unused) else RTS with A = v_ptr+1, C=1, Z=1, N=0 exactly as the old RTS (old A was also v_ptr+1, flags from the same CMP). cells_next_page moves intact (INC v_ptr+1 / BRA cells_on_page); its only reference is BCS cells_next_page in .more, a backward branch of 0xDC bytes-offset (-36), in range. .cells_on_page and everything after .more is untouched.
